This document defines approved patterns for inbound API traffic into Entegris platforms on GCP. It gives architects a consistent way to expose public, partner, and internal APIs while preserving security and operational control. The value of the pattern is speed to execution — leveraging what others have done before and quickly achieving business outcomes A pattern is best expressed as: When to use, When Not to use certain technologies/approaches This document is for designers and architects who need to publish or consume inbound APIs with the correct gateway, protection, and authentication approach If implemented properly, these patterns enable you to get to production as fast as possible and have the most stable, scalable, and maintenance-free set of applications possible

These patterns cover inbound REST-first API exposure for internet-facing, partner, and internal service traffic. External consumer access to Entegris APIs through protected ingress services Partner and internal application-to-application calls into Cloud Run or GKE backends Environments: Cloud Hybrid
Solution Architects Integration Engineers Application Developers Security and Operations Teams

Cloud Armor is mandatory in front of every internet-facing endpoint and must not be bypassed Published APIs require an OpenAPI 3.1 contract and consistent gateway policy enforcement Authentication differs by consumer type: OAuth 2.0/OIDC for user-facing flows and service principal credentials for machine-to-machine access Gateway capabilities such as throttling, routing, and analytics must be centralized in the approved API management layer

Reduce cost through consolidation of functionality Agility through solutions based on a set of services that supports restructuring and reconfiguration of business processes Time-to-market through business-aligned solutions Alignment between IT and business goals, enabling re-use over time
Loosely Coupled and Interoperable Solutions Remove Friction Keep It Simple
Internet and API First Applications Expose Stable, Documented Interfaces Observability and Reliability by Design
Security and Privacy by Design Defense in Depth Security Assurance Through Least Privilege

Solution When to Use When Not to Use Public API Ingress • Need internet-facing access for broad external consumers • Require WAF, DDoS protection, and centralized policy enforcement • Traffic is private-only inside the enterprise network • The API is not ready for formal external publishing and support Partner API Ingress • Need controlled access for a known external organization • Require stronger trust controls such as mTLS and scoped OAuth • Consumers are anonymous or open public users • The partner cannot support required certificate or token standards Internal Service-to-Service • Need service calls between Entegris-managed workloads • Traffic stays on approved private or internal paths • The API must be exposed to internet consumers • A partner or external tenant needs direct access

Scenario Cue Consumer Type Exposure Direction Recommended Pattern Notes Developer-facing external API Public external consumer Internet-facing Consumer → GCP Public API Ingress Use Cloud Armor with approved API gateway (Apigee or Kong per TRB decision); rate limit to 100 req/sec per API key Supplier integration endpoint Named partner organization Internet-facing Partner → GCP Partner API Ingress Implement mTLS with partner-specific client certificates stored in Certificate Manager Internal order service calling pricing service Entegris application Private/internal App → App Internal Service-to-Service Use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for internal APIs requiring Entegris SSO authentication

Area Description Context Entegris exposes a REST API to external consumers over the internet. The API must be resilient, contract-driven, and protected by standard perimeter controls. Problem How do we expose an external API without letting consumers bypass mandatory protection, governance, and backend isolation controls? Solution • Front the endpoint with Google Cloud Armor and an approved API gateway platform such as Apigee or Kong once selected by Entegris • Publish an OpenAPI 3.1 specification and enforce authentication, quotas, and routing policies at the gateway layer • Route traffic to a Cloud Run or GKE backend behind the load balancer so the application is not directly exposed to the internet Benefits • Applies a consistent security and governance posture to all external APIs • Supports rate limiting, analytics, and lifecycle management from a single control point • Decouples consumer-facing contracts from backend implementation details Considerations • User-facing APIs should use OAuth 2.0/OIDC rather than ad hoc authentication schemes • Cloud Armor rules and gateway policies must be tuned together to avoid blocking legitimate traffic

Area Description Context A known partner system needs controlled access to a business API hosted by Entegris. The relationship requires tighter identity controls and supportable operating boundaries. Problem How do we let a partner call an Entegris API while enforcing stronger trust, contractual throttling, and support visibility? Solution • Expose the API through Cloud Armor and the approved gateway with partner-specific routing and policy enforcement • Require mTLS or OAuth 2.0 client credentials with a service principal based trust model appropriate to the partner integration • Route the request to a backend on Cloud Run or GKE and include correlation IDs for end-to-end tracing Benefits • Supports secure partner onboarding with explicit policy boundaries • Makes quota, certificate, and scope management visible and auditable • Keeps backend services isolated from direct partner connectivity Considerations • Certificate lifecycle and partner credential rotation need an agreed operational process • Partner-specific exceptions should be modeled as gateway policy, not custom backend logic

Area Description Context Two Entegris-managed workloads need machine-to-machine API communication inside the enterprise boundary. The goal is low-latency access without unnecessary internet exposure. Problem How do we support internal API calls while preserving service identity, least privilege, and operational traceability? Solution • Use approved internal routing such as service mesh or direct private access to a Cloud Run or GKE backend • Authenticate machine-to-machine traffic with service principal client credentials or equivalent non-user identity controls • Apply contract, logging, and monitoring standards even when the API is not internet-facing Benefits • Reduces exposure surface compared with public ingress patterns • Supports efficient low-latency calls between internal services • Preserves identity-based authorization and operational observability Considerations • Internal APIs still need versioning and OpenAPI contracts when they are reused across teams • Do not treat private networking as a substitute for authentication and authorization

Use Cloud Armor WAF policies managed in Terraform, never manual Console changes Store API keys in GCP Secret Manager and rotate every 90 days minimum Log all API requests to Cloud Logging with correlation_id for distributed tracing Set Cloud Armor rate limits to 100 requests/sec per client IP by default Use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for internal APIs requiring Entegris SSO authentication

documents.t: This document defines an initial Entegris pattern for enterprise file share access and integration. It gives teams a standard path to onboard a file-share-enabled application with SSO, entitlement governance, and controlled application access. The value of the pattern is speed to execution — leveraging what others have done before and quickly achieving business outcomes A pattern is best expressed as: When to use, When Not to use certain technologies/approaches This document is for designers and architects who need to enable user and system access to enterprise file shares without bypassing identity, security, and governance controls If implemented properly, these patterns enable teams to move quickly while preserving least privilege, auditability, and supportability

These patterns cover user and application access to enterprise file share platforms with Entra ID, SAML SSO, Access Packages, and governed service-to-service integration. Human user access through SAML SSO and Access Package assignment Application access through Entra ID app registration, App ID, and service principal permissions Optional ingestion of file-share content into enterprise platforms using approved middleware Environments: SaaS Cloud Hybrid
Solution Architects Application Engineers Integration Engineers Identity and Access Teams Security and Operations Teams

New app access to file-share resources requires an App ID (Entra ID app registration) if one does not already exist Human user access must use federated SSO through Entra ID and governed entitlement assignment through Access Packages Service-to-service access must use a managed application identity and least-privilege scopes; shared credentials and user accounts are not approved Requests for SAML, Access Package, and onboarding workflow are routed through standard ServiceNow intake with Identity team guidance Human review remains required for material data publication or externally shared outputs generated from file-share content

Standardizes onboarding steps across architecture, identity, and operations Reduces delays from ad hoc access requests and one-off identity configurations Improves auditability of who can access what, and why Lowers security risk through least-privilege and centralized identity governance
Keep It Simple Reuse Shared Application Services First Remove Friction
Applications Expose Stable, Documented Interfaces Single Source of Truth Humans in the Loop for Material Decisions
Security and Privacy by Design Security Assurance Through Least Privilege Defense in Depth

This pattern is constrained by the following guidance: User-facing authentication must be federated SSO through Entra ID Entitlements must be governed through Access Packages and reviewable group-based access Application integration must use an App ID and service principal with narrowly scoped permissions No shared user credentials, no hardcoded secrets, and no unmanaged local bypass Access grants, application permissions, and administrative actions must be auditable

Solution When to Use When Not to Use SAML + Access Package User Access Pattern • Users need interactive file-share access in a browser or enterprise app • Access must be approved, reviewable, and revocable through standard governance • Team wants direct local accounts or unmanaged identity flows • Access cannot be mapped to reviewable business roles App ID Service Integration Pattern • An application needs machine access to file-share data for read/write automation • Permissions can be scoped to defined sites, folders, or resources • Integration requires broad tenant-wide permissions without business justification • Team plans to use a user credential, shared account, or embedded secret Managed File Share Ingestion Pattern • Need scheduled or event-driven extraction of approved file-share content into enterprise data platforms • Team needs retry, logging, and checkpointing controls • Data movement bypasses approved middleware, security, or landing-zone controls • Team cannot support operational monitoring and replay

Area Description Context A business app needs user access to file-share content, and access must be granted by business role with centralized identity governance. Problem How do we enable fast user onboarding while enforcing enterprise SSO and entitlement controls? Solution • Integrate the application with Entra ID for SAML SSO and disable local authentication paths • Define role-based groups and publish Access Packages aligned to business roles and approval flows • Route onboarding via ServiceNow request with Identity team review, including access owner, approver, and periodic recertification requirements Benefits • Consistent user login and lifecycle management across enterprise applications • Reviewable and revocable access through centralized entitlement governance • Lower operational risk from ad hoc manual user provisioning Considerations • Role and entitlement design quality drives usability and supportability • Group and Access Package ownership must be explicit to avoid stale access

documents.t: Area Description Context An application or integration service requires non-interactive access to file-share resources. Problem How do we provide machine access without using user credentials or over-scoped permissions? Solution • Create or reuse a governed Entra ID app registration (App ID) with named ownership and business purpose • Use service principal authentication and request only required permissions for the specific file-share scope • Store client credentials or certificates in approved secret management and implement rotation, logging, and access review controls Benefits • Eliminates dependency on personal user accounts for system integrations • Enables least-privilege, auditable, and revocable service access • Aligns service authentication to enterprise identity and risk processes Considerations • Permission expansion requires explicit review and change control • Certificate and secret rotation must be operationalized before go-live

Area Description Context Teams need approved file-share content moved into enterprise processing platforms for analytics, workflow, or indexing. Problem How do we ingest content reliably while preserving security boundaries and replayability? Solution • Use approved middleware to orchestrate extraction, checkpointing, retries, and failure handling • Authenticate through App ID service principal and pull only approved paths/content classes • Land raw content in the approved landing zone first, then perform downstream transformation with lineage metadata Benefits • Improves reliability through standardized retry and checkpoint controls • Preserves traceability from source file to downstream record • Reduces custom one-off ingestion scripts and support burden Considerations • Event and delta logic requires careful handling of deletes, renames, and replay windows • Data classification and retention obligations apply to copied content

Control Area Required Direction for File Share Patterns Authentication Use Entra ID SAML SSO for users and service principal identity for machine integrations; no local auth schemes. Entitlement Governance Use Access Packages and role-based group assignment with owner/approver accountability and periodic reviews. Application Identity Ensure App ID exists with named owner, documented purpose, and scoped permissions. Secrets Management Store credentials/certificates in approved secret management; no hardcoded or shared credentials. Least Privilege Grant only required scopes/resources; avoid wildcard or tenant-wide permissions unless explicitly approved. Logging and Audit Log access requests, grants, scope changes, and integration actions with correlation IDs; do not log sensitive content bodies by default. Data Handling Apply data classification, retention, and minimization; do not move restricted data without explicit approval. Operational Support Define ownership for access lifecycle, secret/cert rotation, incident response, and decommissioning.

This document defines approved patterns for integrating Entegris applications and platforms with SAP systems. It helps teams choose the right SAP interaction style based on transactionality, volume, latency, and SAP-native interface options. The value of the pattern is speed to execution — leveraging what others have done before and quickly achieving business outcomes A pattern is best expressed as: When to use, When Not to use certain technologies/approaches This document is for designers and architects who need to integrate with SAP using the right middleware, protocol, and operational model for each business scenario If implemented properly, these patterns enable you to get to production as fast as possible and have the most stable, scalable, and maintenance-free set of applications possible

These patterns cover synchronous, batch, SAP-native, and asynchronous integration approaches between SAP and the broader Entegris estate. SAP request/reply, batch, and event-style integrations mediated through approved middleware Use of SAP-native interfaces such as IDoc, RFC/BAPI, and OData for standardized connectivity Environments: Cloud Hybrid
Solution Architects Integration Engineers SAP Engineers Security and Operations Teams

Boomi is the standard middleware for SAP integration across most scenarios Aecorsoft is approved only for large-volume SAP data loads where Boomi is not appropriate Boomi SAP adapters should be preferred over custom connectivity when a standard interface is available BTP may be used for more complex custom interfaces that cannot be met with standard adapter patterns

Reduce cost through consolidation of functionality Agility through solutions based on a set of services that supports restructuring and reconfiguration of business processes Time-to-market through business-aligned solutions Alignment between IT and business goals, enabling re-use over time

Single ERP, Minimal Customization Integration Through Standard Middleware Single Source of Truth

Solution When to Use When Not to Use Synchronous API (Request/Reply) • Need immediate business response from SAP • Volume is moderate and user or process flow is latency-sensitive • The use case is high-volume batch extraction • Long-running processing would cause timeouts or poor user experience Batch SFTP (File-based Extract/Load) • Need scheduled large-file exchange with SAP or adjacent systems • Payloads are naturally file-oriented • The use case requires immediate interactive response • The data volume is so large that Aecorsoft should be used instead Batch API (Scheduled Extract/Load) • Need scheduled integration through API-style calls • Business latency is measured in batch windows • Real-time transactional interaction is required • Repeated polling would create unnecessary load or poor fit SAP IDoc / RFC / OData (SAP-native) • Need a standard SAP-native interface for document, function, or REST-style integration • A Boomi SAP adapter or approved SAP capability exists • Teams want to build custom Z endpoints without exhausting standard options • The interface style is mismatched to the SAP business object behavior Asynchronous Pattern (Fire-and-forget / event-triggered) • Need decoupled processing with eventual consistency • SAP does not need to respond in-line to the caller • The business operation requires immediate synchronous confirmation • Consumers cannot handle eventual consistency or delayed failure handling

Scenario Cue Interaction Type Volume Direction Recommended Pattern Notes Customer lookup during order entry Synchronous request/reply Low to moderate App ↔ SAP Synchronous API (Request/Reply) Use Boomi SAP adapter with 30-second timeout; implement fallback to cached data for resilience Large nightly material master extract Batch file transfer Very high SAP → GCP Batch SFTP (File-based Extract/Load) Use Aecorsoft (not Boomi) when volume exceeds 100K records or 1GB file size Scheduled pull of standard SAP dataset Batch API polling Moderate SAP → GCP Batch API (Scheduled Extract/Load) Run during SAP batch windows (8pm-6am PST) to avoid peak production load Standard order document exchange SAP-native async or function call Moderate SAP ↔ Enterprise SAP IDoc / RFC / OData (SAP-native) Use standard IDoc types (ORDERS05, MATMAS05) before creating custom Z interfaces Event-driven outbound notification Asynchronous fire-and-forget Moderate SAP → Consumer Asynchronous Pattern (Fire-and-forget / event-triggered) Publish SAP events to Pub/Sub with message deduplication enabled to handle retries

Area Description Context A business process or user interaction needs an immediate response from SAP before it can continue. The integration must be reliable enough for in-line execution. Problem How do we call SAP synchronously without bypassing middleware, losing observability, or creating duplicate transactional side effects? Solution • Use Boomi as the mediation layer for synchronous request/reply interactions between the caller and SAP • Prefer standard SAP interfaces exposed through approved adapters or APIs that match the required business function • Propagate correlation IDs and design retries carefully so transient failures do not create duplicate writes Benefits • Supports business flows that need immediate confirmation from SAP • Keeps middleware governance, logging, and policy enforcement in the path • Allows consistent operational support with traceable transaction context Considerations • Long-running SAP operations may not fit synchronous user or API timeout limits • Write operations must account for atomic commit behavior and safe retry design

Area Description Context A SAP integration exchanges large datasets on a scheduled basis and file-oriented transfer is the natural contract. Operations teams need clear handoff points and reconciliation. Problem How do we move scheduled SAP files safely and at scale without forcing interactive or chatty API patterns onto a batch workload? Solution • Use a managed file exchange pattern mediated through the approved integration platform and secure transport such as SFTP • Select Aecorsoft only for large-volume SAP loads where Boomi is not the right operational or performance fit • Track file receipt, processing status, and replay metadata so batch support teams can reconcile each transfer Benefits • Fits large scheduled extracts and loads cleanly • Provides explicit operational checkpoints for reconciliation and reprocessing • Avoids forcing high-volume workloads through inappropriate synchronous designs Considerations • File contracts and encryption practices must be governed carefully with SAP and downstream owners • Very high-volume interfaces should be justified explicitly when selecting Aecorsoft over Boomi

Area Description Context A SAP dataset can be retrieved or loaded on a schedule through API-oriented interaction rather than file exchange. The business process tolerates batch latency. Problem How do we use scheduled SAP APIs efficiently without creating needless polling load or hiding failures in custom scripts? Solution • Use Boomi and the SAP adapter to execute scheduled extract or load operations against approved SAP APIs • Align schedules to business windows and API capacity so loads are predictable and supportable • Persist run state, correlation IDs, and response outcomes for replay and operational troubleshooting Benefits • Supports batch semantics while retaining API-level structure and middleware governance • Reduces the operational overhead of bespoke scripts • Improves consistency of logging, retry, and error routing Considerations • Polling schedules should be reviewed to ensure a true event or native SAP interface would not be a better fit • Large dataset pagination and timeout handling require careful design

Area Description Context The business object or process maps naturally to a standard SAP-native integration interface. Entegris wants to maximize supportability and minimize unnecessary custom SAP endpoints. Problem How do we choose and use the right SAP-native interface while preserving standardization and avoiding unnecessary custom development? Solution • Use Boomi SAP adapters with standard SAP-native interfaces such as IDoc for document exchange, RFC/BAPI for function calls, or OData for RESTful access • Select the interface style that best matches the business semantic and processing pattern rather than forcing one style everywhere • Avoid custom Z endpoints unless a documented business need remains after evaluating the standard SAP options and BTP alternatives Benefits • Improves compatibility with standard SAP capabilities and support models • Reduces custom integration maintenance over time • Helps align interface choice to native SAP business semantics Considerations • Teams need SAP-specific expertise to choose the right interface for each business object and transaction • Custom extensions should go through stronger architecture review because they increase lifecycle cost

Area Description Context A process can continue without waiting for SAP to respond in-line and eventual consistency is acceptable. Decoupling improves resilience and throughput for the business flow. Problem How do we integrate with SAP asynchronously while preserving reliability, idempotency, and operational visibility? Solution • Publish the request or event through Boomi using an asynchronous design and let SAP process it out of band • Carry correlation IDs and idempotency keys so retries or duplicate deliveries can be detected safely • Monitor acknowledgements, failures, and compensating actions through structured logs and operational dashboards Benefits • Improves resilience by decoupling the initiating process from SAP availability and latency • Supports higher throughput for non-interactive workloads • Fits document-style or event-driven enterprise integration scenarios well Considerations • Business teams must understand and accept eventual consistency behavior • Failure handling requires clear ownership when the initiating caller is no longer waiting synchronously

Store SAP credentials in GCP Secret Manager with automatic rotation every 90 days Use Aecorsoft for batch extracts exceeding 100K records; use Boomi for transactional flows under 10K records Log all IDoc and BAPI correlation IDs to Cloud Logging for SAP troubleshooting Land raw SAP payloads in GCS Bronze before any transformation to preserve audit trail Test SAP integrations in Sandbox first, then Dev, then Prod - never skip environments

This document defines approved patterns for ingesting SharePoint Online content into the Entegris GCP data platform using Microsoft Graph API and Boomi. It helps teams choose the fastest compliant path for list, library, and document ingestion. The value of the pattern is speed to execution — leveraging what others have done before and quickly achieving business outcomes A pattern is best expressed as: When to use, When Not to use certain technologies/approaches This document is for designers and architects who need to move SharePoint Online content into GCP without violating Entegris integration, identity, and landing-zone standards If implemented properly, these patterns enable you to get to production as fast as possible and have the most stable, scalable, and maintenance-free set of applications possible

These patterns cover SharePoint Online ingestion scenarios that must land raw data in Entegris-managed GCP services. Scheduled extraction of SharePoint lists, libraries, and document metadata Change-aware ingestion using Microsoft Graph delta queries and webhook notifications Environments: SaaS Hybrid Cloud
Solution Architects Integration Engineers Data Engineers Security and Operations Teams

Entegris standardizes on Microsoft Graph API; direct SharePoint REST API usage is not approved Authentication must use an Entra ID app registration and service principal with client credentials grant, never a user account Boomi is the approved orchestration layer for retries, scheduling, and error handling All raw payloads and files must land first in a GCS Bronze bucket before downstream transformation

Solution When to Use When Not to Use Batch Ingestion • Need scheduled full or targeted extracts from lists and libraries • Freshness is hourly, daily, or otherwise time-based • Need near-real-time updates • Cannot tolerate scanning unchanged items repeatedly Incremental/Delta Ingestion • Need changed items only to reduce API calls and processing cost • Can persist and manage the Microsoft Graph delta token • Source objects do not support the needed delta query behavior • Team cannot operationally manage token lifecycle and replay logic Event-triggered Ingestion • Need rapid awareness of changes or uploads • Can manage SharePoint webhook subscription renewal and validation • Need guaranteed delivery of full payload directly from the event • Source system or process cannot support webhook governance

Scenario Cue Frequency Volume Auth Method Direction Recommended Pattern Notes Daily document archive from a library Scheduled Large Entra ID service principal + client credentials SharePoint → GCP Batch Ingestion Use Boomi with Graph API batch endpoints when fetching >1000 items to stay under throttling limits Hourly updates for active list items Scheduled delta Small to medium Entra ID service principal + client credentials SharePoint → GCP Incremental/Delta Ingestion Store delta tokens in Boomi Process Property or GCS to enable replay after failures Immediate notification when a file is added Event-triggered Small to medium Entra ID service principal + client credentials SharePoint → GCP Event-triggered Ingestion Webhook subscriptions expire after 6 months - implement auto-renewal in Boomi scheduled process

Area Description Context Business teams store documents and metadata in SharePoint Online that must be copied to GCP on a scheduled cadence. The downstream platform expects raw content in Bronze before any cleansing. Problem How do we ingest SharePoint data on a predictable schedule using Entegris-standard authentication, middleware, and landing zones? Solution • Use Microsoft Graph API endpoints such as https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{site}/lists/{list}/items from a Boomi process scheduled by business cadence • Authenticate with an Entra ID app registration and service principal using client credentials grant with least-privilege scopes such as Sites.Read.All or Files.Read.All • Store raw responses and file payloads unchanged in a GCS Bronze bucket and let downstream pipelines promote data to Silver Benefits • Simple to operate and easy to align with batch business processes • Centralizes retry, paging, and error handling in Boomi • Keeps the ingestion path compliant with the Entegris raw-landing model Considerations • Full scans can increase API consumption and processing cost for large sites • Schedule-based latency may be too slow for urgent downstream actions

Area Description Context SharePoint content changes frequently, but only changed records need to be processed between runs. Teams want lower cost and faster refresh than a full extraction. Problem How do we pull only changed SharePoint items without losing state across retries and restarts? Solution • Call Microsoft Graph delta query endpoints from Boomi and capture only changed or deleted items since the previous successful execution • Persist the delta token in a durable store managed by the integration solution so the next run resumes from the correct checkpoint • Write changed payloads to GCS Bronze with idempotent object naming so replays do not create downstream duplicates Benefits • Reduces API calls and execution time compared with full loads • Improves freshness while preserving scheduled control points • Supports scalable ingestion of active lists and libraries Considerations • Token lifecycle, expiry, and recovery logic must be designed and tested carefully • Deletes and schema changes need explicit downstream handling

Area Description Context A business process needs prompt downstream handling when SharePoint content changes. The notification is event-driven, but the content still needs to be fetched through Graph API. Problem How do we trigger ingestion quickly from SharePoint changes while staying within Entegris middleware and security standards? Solution • Register a SharePoint webhook that notifies a Boomi endpoint when subscribed content changes • Validate the webhook handshake and use Boomi to fetch the changed item details through Microsoft Graph API with a service principal • Land the fetched content in GCS Bronze and record correlation details for replay and operational support Benefits • Provides faster response to content changes than schedule-only patterns • Limits Graph reads to changed items after an event occurs • Fits event-driven business workflows while retaining Boomi governance Considerations • Webhook subscriptions require renewal, monitoring, and fallback handling • Notifications are triggers, so the integration must still retrieve the authoritative payload from Graph API

Store Graph API credentials in GCP Secret Manager, never in Boomi profiles or environment variables Use Boomi's built-in retry logic with exponential backoff for Graph API throttling (429 errors) Log all correlation IDs to Cloud Logging for end-to-end traceability from Graph API to GCS Bronze Partition BigQuery tables by ingestion_date from day one to control query costs Register one Entra ID service principal per integration domain for reviewable and revocable permissions

This policy enables Entegris to embrace AI technologies by offering clear guidance for using AI solutions securely and responsibly. It is the principle of Entegris to support and promote the use of AI technologies to improve productivity and performance, so that we may better serve our customers and deliver value to the marketplace. This policy is intended to encourage employees to confidently embrace AI technologies. It applies to all AI use that interacts with Entegris data, systems or workflows. Authorized AI tools may be used with Entegris confidential information (excluding confidential-restricted data) without further approval. Before entering confidential-restricted data in authorized AI tools, consult with the Law Department first.

This policy applies to anyone using AI technologies in connection with Entegris-related work. This includes, but is not limited to, employees, contractors, consultants, interns, MSPs, and third-party vendors. It governs AI technologies and usage on any device, network or system where the activity involves Entegris data, systems or business processes. 2.1 The scope of this policy covers all such technological solutions that incorporate artificial intelligence capabilities, such as: General AI services 3rd party services available for the company to use Agentic AI agents All internally developed Generative AI models 2.2 This is an Entegris Global policy.

Executive Leadership (as defined in Career Framework) Set strategic direction for AI adoption and governance. Champion responsible AI uses across the organization. Enforce the AI policy and ensure alignment with company values and risk appetite. Identify appropriate AI use cases within their departments. Ensure staff are trained in responsible AI use. Report incidents or misuse of AI tools. Cybersecurity team and IT Strategic Platforms team Monitor regulatory developments and ensure policy compliance. Define acceptable use and prohibited practices. Conduct risk assessments for AI systems and integrations. Publish the list of Authorized AI tools. Cybersecurity Risk Management team Establish process to conduct risk assessments of AI technologies and Agentic AI solutions. Where the AI solution is from a 3rd party provider (supplier/vendor), conduct vendor due diligence in accordance with Supplier Risk Management policy requirements. Prepare reports on AI solution suppliers' risk profiles, and risks associated with specific Agentic AI agents, and share with Leadership on a periodic basis. Manage all risk exceptions related to AI technologies and Agentic AI solutions implemented. Procurement Conduct comprehensive vendor due diligence for all AI solution providers and AI procurement requests consistent with generally applicable procurement standards and business processes, including financial stability reviews and regulatory compliance verification. Ensure all AI procurement activities comply with applicable procurement policies. Negotiate and execute contracts with AI vendors that include appropriate data protection, confidentiality, and liability limitations.

Term Definition Artificial Intelligence (AI) Machine-based systems that simulate human intelligence to perform tasks (like learning, reasoning, understanding language, recognizing patterns, making predictions, generating content, and decision-making) by analyzing data. Authorized AI tools AI tools that have been reviewed and approved in writing by the Law Department, the IT Technology Review Board (TRB), the IT Architecture Review Board (ARB) and Executive Leadership for the Division or Department. These tools are developed internally or licensed or purchased through the Procurement team and configured for enterprise use. These tools are hosted on internal servers or approved cloud platforms with data protection agreements. Confidential Restricted Data that is "Confidential Restricted" pursuant to the Entegris Confidential Information Policy. This is a subset of Confidential Information which is accessible, shared, or disclosed only to a very limited and small set of Entegris Employees who have a critical need to know such information within the scope of their employment and obligations at Entegris. Please review Entegris' Confidential Information Policy for the full definition of Confidential Restricted. Confidential Restricted information should not be input, uploaded or processed using an AI tool. Public AI tools AI platforms available to the general public that have not been formally approved by Entegris. This includes free, trial or personal-use versions of tools like ChatGPT Free, Google Gemini, Claude or Microsoft Copilot used via personal accounts. This list is not exhaustive, as the public tools available in the marketplace will change. Training Data The dataset used to teach an AI model how to recognize patterns and make predictions.

The below listed documents will provide additional information related to this policy's requirements: Entegris Code of Business Ethics Confidential Information Policy Entegris Data Classification Standard #13833 Entegris Technology Acceptable Use Policy #10784 Entegris Cybersecurity Policy #47907 Entegris Supplier Cybersecurity Risk Management policy

Only authorized AI tools are permitted for work-related tasks. These tools must be: Provisioned through official channels Configured for enterprise use Equipped with appropriate access, logging, and data handling controls Use of unauthorized AI tools for Entegris work purposes is strictly prohibited, and such AI tools must never be provided with access to Entegris' Confidential and Confidential Restricted information. 6.1.1 Acceptable uses​ All use of artificial intelligence solutions must comply with the guidelines outlined in the Entegris Technology Acceptable Use policy, and adhere to Confidential Information Policy and Data Classification standards. Given below is a list of acceptable uses: Drafting and Content Support: Assisting with internal communications, documentation, presentations, templates, generating educational materials, FAQs, or simulations using approved datasets. Process and Workflow Efficiency: Supporting internal tasks such as summarizing information, formatting documents, organizing notes, or prepopulating forms or survey questionnaires and assessments. AI must not execute decisions or actions without human oversight. Predictive Maintenance: Using predictive AI tools to plan for and schedule maintenance of tools and equipment. Quality Control / Defect Detection: Using AI vision to identify anomalies to assist in the detection of defects in manufacturing earlier than manual inspection. Supply chain and inventory optimization: Use of AI tools to forecast demand, supplier risks, and logistics routing. R&D Acceleration / Knowledge Work Support: Use of AI tools to assist researchers and engineers in development of intellectual property, exploring literature, generating design alternatives, designing experiments, automating routine analysis. Process Simulation and Optimization: Use of AI tools to simulate to optimize business processes. Data Review & Research: Summarizing documents, identifying patterns in unclassified data, or supporting internal/public research. Outputs used in decision-making must be validated by a qualified human reviewer. Note: No autonomous (agentic) AI agents may be used in production until it passes human review, validated testing, and a documented security review via formal change control.

Users must keep in mind that AI tools pose potential data privacy and compliance risks. To protect Entegris data, users should follow these guidelines: 6.2.1 Human Accountability: AI-generated content must be reviewed by the user for accuracy, appropriateness and compliance with company standards. Final responsibility for the content rests with the human user, not the tool. 6.2.2 Sensitive Data Restrictions: Unless explicitly authorized by the Law Department, users must not input sensitive data (such as credentials, payment information, or personally identifiable information like social security numbers and bank account numbers) into any AI tool (including Authorized AI tools). 6.2.3 External communication restrictions: AI-generated output intended for regulators or other external governing bodies must undergo review and approval by a member of Executive Leadership (as that term is defined within the Career Framework) prior to release of the information and is subject to the "Communications with External Parties" section of the Code of Business Ethics.

The following uses of AI tools are strictly prohibited, regardless of whether the tool is public, personal, or Entegris approved: 6.3.1 Use of AI other than Authorized AI Tools: Use of any AI tool which is not an Authorized AI tool for Entegris business is not permitted. 6.3.2 Handling Confidential-Restricted and other sensitive data: Users must not input, upload, or process Confidential-Restricted data using any AI tool. Users must not input sensitive information (such as credentials, payment information, or personally identifiable information like social security numbers and bank account numbers) into any AI tool. 6.3.3 Autonomous actions or automation without oversight: AI tools may not send messages, make decisions, approve financial transactions, execute scripts or perform tasks on behalf of Entegris without direct human initiation and oversight. Automated use must be reviewed and approved in writing by a member of Executive Leadership representing the division or department as well as Cybersecurity and IT Strategic Platforms teams. 6.3.4 Impersonation or misrepresentation: AI tools may not be used to mimic or impersonate employees, customers, vendors or regulators in any format, including written, visual, audio or synthetic media in a deceptive fashion or without consent. 6.3.5 Unsafe, or unlawful output: Users must not use AI tools to generate content that violates legal requirements or our Code of Business Ethics. AI-generated content must not be relied on in ways that may cause harm to Entegris or violate the rights of Entegris' customers or other third parties. 6.3.6 Bypassing corporate controls: Users must not use personal devices, incognito browsers, proxies, VPNs, or alternate tools to bypass corporate policies or restrictions on AI usage. Enabling experimental features, plug-ins, or agentic behavior in AI tools without prior approval is a violation of this policy.

All individuals using AI tools for work must adhere to the following responsibilities to ensure safe, compliant, and effective use: 6.4.1 New tools may be submitted for review by the ARB and TRB by submitting a request through the Company's Enterprise Architecture Ensider page. Only Authorized AI tools shall be deployed for use related to Entegris' business. 6.4.2 Users must review and approve all AI-generated content before using or sharing it, ensuring outputs are accurate, appropriate, and aligned with business objectives. 6.4.3 Where transparency is required by law, users must clearly disclose when content has been assisted by AI, in line with legal obligations. 6.4.4 Users should complete AI tool training prior to use, and should stay informed about evolving policies, tool capabilities, and approved use cases. 6.4.5 If an AI tool behaves unexpectedly, produces inappropriate content or is suspected of misusing data, users must report the issue immediately to the AI tool owner and/or Cybersecurity, for further action and escalation. 6.4.6 Any suspected misuse must be reported immediately to the AI Tool Owner or Application Owner.

6.5.1 AI tools, whether public or approved, must be regarded as potential data processors. Prompts and other inputs may be subject to discovery during litigation or investigations. Any interaction with these systems, including inputs and outputs, can pose privacy, confidentiality, and compliance risks. 6.5.2 Existing data classification policies defined in the Entegris Confidential Information Policy apply to the use of AI tools. Users may not attempt to bypass these policies by masking or altering confidential information for AI input unless they have approval from a member of Executive Leadership (as defined in the Career Framework) to do so. Even redacted content can carry risks and should be handled with caution. 6.5.4 Outputs generated by AI tools must be reviewed carefully, especially if they summarize internal documents, describe proprietary workflows or may contain inferred confidential details. Outputs should not be shared, stored or reused in ways that could expose confidential information to third parties not covered by a non-disclosure agreement. 6.5.5 Users should assume that any prompt or response sent to an AI tool may be discoverable by external parties, and may be retained, reused or analyzed by the provider. Even with Approved AI tools, users are responsible for understanding the provider's data retention policies. 6.5.6 To ensure that all AI-related activities comply with the GDPR data minimization principle (i.e., that only relevant and necessary data may be retained), prompts and related data should not be stored beyond the active processing session unless necessary. If temporary retention is required, prompts and other inputs should be retained for the shortest possible duration, not exceeding 7 days unless a Data Protection Impact Assessment or legal hold justifies a longer period. Systems should be configured to automatically delete all prompt data upon task completion or at the expiry of the retention period.

6.6.1 AI activity conducted through company-licensed AI tools may be monitored and logged in accordance with applicable laws. 6.6.2 Attempts to bypass monitoring controls (by using personal accounts, private browsing modes, unauthorized devices or unapproved tools) are policy violations. 6.6.3 Monitoring and logging of AI tool usage will be implemented in alignment with approved business use cases and technical capabilities. Until such controls are in place, users are expected to follow approved data handling practices. 6.6.4 Prompts and related data will be retained only as long as necessary for operational or business purposes. Operational prompts should not exceed 7 days unless justified by a DPIA or legal hold. Business-critical prompts and configuration settings may be retained for up to 90 days. All retention is subject to legal hold requirements, which override these limits.

Users should assume that any prompt may be discoverable by third parties, including adversaries in the event of litigation or regulators in the event of government investigations. All users must strictly comply with the guidelines below: 6.7.1 Unsafe, or unlawful output: Users must not use AI tools to generate content that violates legal or regulatory requirements or our Code of Business Ethics. AI-generated content must not be relied on in ways that violate the cause harm to Entegris or violates the rights of Entegris' customers or third parties. 6.7.2 Users are required by Entegris' Code of Business Ethics to offer their full, timely and truthful cooperation with all investigations.

6.8.1 Non-compliance with this policy, including intentional misuse, negligence, or unauthorized experimentation may result in disciplinary action. 6.8.2 All suspected violations will be reviewed by the appropriate internal teams, including Cybersecurity, Legal, HR and/or Compliance. Users are expected to cooperate fully with any investigations. Where required, incidents involving AI misuse may be escalated to external authorities or regulators in accordance with applicable laws and contractual obligations. 6.8.3 Entegris will develop and publish additional policies and standards to support implementation of this policy.

It is expected that all information technology and operational technology teams in Entegris will follow this policy's requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business/Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented as per the Entegris Exception Management Process.

All security related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. IT/OT Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies will be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

This policy governs the cybersecurity of all Entegris information technology (IT) assets and systems, including both Hardware and Software, across IT and operational technology (OT) environments. This policy is required because technology assets and information systems deployed at Entegris contain confidential, proprietary, and competitive information which is critical to our manufacturing operations and overall success in the marketplace. These information systems and assets must be safeguarded and kept secure from both internal and external threats.

Entegris depends on its information systems for all its operations as they are the backbone for keeping a competitive edge in the market. Hence, security and risk management of all information systems is vital to our growth and continued viability as a successful business entity. Any attack on our systems can lead to loss of production, potentially lead to severe financial losses or reputational damage, and impact on our customer relations. Hence, it is imperative for us to ensure all Entegris technology assets and information systems are monitored and safeguarded from these attacks.

The policy applies globally to all Entegris sites and facilities. Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility. The involvement and participation of all Entegris employees, contractors and third-party service providers is essential to successfully implementing this policy. Hence this policy applies to all Entegris employees, contractors and service providers. This policy is applicable to all IT and OT assets and systems.

Chief Information Officer Responsible for protecting all Entegris Information Technology assets and systems Responsible for establishing Information Security policy and implementation of it Establish information security organization and provide resources for its effective operation Provide updates to Board of Directors on Entegris Cybersecurity posture, potential threats and risk mitigations Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) Manage Cyber Security policy and ensure cybersecurity and risk management program is operational and effective Establish and manage Cybersecurity Awareness and Education programs across the organization Equip and enable Business Leaders to understand cyber security control requirements, alternative controls, and clearly identify areas of responsibility to manage their critical assets, and help businesses to raise policy exceptions based on business justification Follows-up with Business Leaders to ensure cyber security controls are implemented and risks are mitigated in a timely manner Communicate information security related risks and overall security posture to executive leadership Review Exception requests coming from Business teams, if necessary, provide feedback or escalate. As system and data systems custodians across Entegris, Information Technology will deploy cybersecurity policies and protocols globally, covering various security control domains, as listed below:

Entegris must establish and implement an Asset Management policy that provides clear guidance on assets procurement, lifecycle management, and sunsetting of assets. In addition, the policy must define requirements on establishing a central asset management repository, and guidelines on asset classification and controls, and ongoing asset monitoring requirements.

6.2.1 Access to Entegris systems and networks – physical access to Entegris data centers, servers, networks and to our endpoint devices (inclusive of laptops and mobile devices) should be restricted to only authorized persons. 6.2.2 Physical Access to Data Centers and System Servers – Entegris Site management in conjunction with Entegris Global EHS must ensure that only authorized users will have physical access to IT Data Centers-and network closets, and other critical file cabinets, etc. 6.2.3 Physical Access for Endpoint Devices – Entegris Global EHS shall publish and communicate physical security guidelines to all Entegris users on how to protect the endpoint devices assigned to them.

Access to Entegris data and applications must adhere to the following access management controls: 6.3.1 Define and enforce policies that restrict access to systems and data based on roles, attributes, and contextual factors. Implementation and enforcement of access management policies that govern the identification, authentication, and authorization of users and systems to access organizational resources. 6.3.2 Access to applications and other systems must be given through appropriate approvals and establishing baseline access controls. 6.3.3 Controls such as, Account Management, Access Enforcement, Password standards, multi-factor authentication, Least Privilege, Remote Access, and Access Control for Mobile Devices must be established. 6.3.4 Entegris must adopt Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) or Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) models to assign permissions 6.3.5 Audit and Accountability (AU) - Log access events and monitor for unauthorized access attempts. 6.3.6 Ensure that access rights are reviewed periodically and updated, as necessary. 6.3.7 Policy Enforcement and Decision Points - Implement Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs) and Policy Decision Points (PDPs) to evaluate and enforce access decisions dynamically.

Entegris will provide standard, supported solutions for business related storage, sharing and collaboration of files. With those solutions in place, data should not be copied to USB drives from corporate issued PCs (laptops and desktops) or copy or forward to personal emails or personal public cloud storage.

All IT assets must be protected with anti-malware and antivirus software, installed and maintained by Global IT to safeguard against computer viruses and other forms of malicious code. 6.5.1 Entegris Cybersecurity teams must develop and implement software vulnerabilities management policies, processes and tools. 6.5.2 The Entegris Sourcing, Cybersecurity, and Global Service Desk must ensure that all software products procured from vendors are chosen following Entegris solution selection process, and are defect free and tested for vulnerabilities prior to installation in the Entegris Environment. 6.5.3 Any software developed by Entegris, either in-house or by its 3rd parties, for use in Entegris products shall be developed using Secure Software Development practices and must be tested for vulnerabilities prior to shipping to Customers. To the extent possible, all custom-built software should use an Entegris controlled code repository and enforce version control processes.

Entegris shall develop a network security policy and implement it to protect Entegris networks from unauthorized access and ensure that the network infrastructure meets Entegris business needs. Entegris shall develop network security architecture that protects its networks integrity by incorporating proper network segmentation, where appropriate, to segregate networks and limit network breach propagation. IT and OT networks will be separated and network traffic traversing between those environments and within the OT network will be highly controlled to protect the integrity of our plant systems.

Entegris technology teams shall develop standards, procedures, tools and job aids to ensure IT and OT hardware systems and components meet Entegris Cybersecurity and operational requirements. These should include product selection criteria, vendor’s design/development practices, product verification & testing, and integration requirements. Entegris shall also establish configuration management and hardening practices for the security of all the device/systems software through the supported product life.

Access to Entegris technology systems and networks shall be monitored at all times and access logs shall be maintained. Any anomalies in individual access should be investigated. All access logs must be immutable and retained for a period consistent with data retention requirements.

All changes to the information systems and IT assets must be controlled and governed. Any proposed technology changes should go through a Change Control process, risk-assessment, and changes implemented in a controlled manner that limits disruption to business operations.

Entegris shall establish a comprehensive incident management and response program to ensure the timely identification, handling, and resolution of cybersecurity and related incidents. This program will aim to minimize disruption to Entegris technology environments and ensure compliance with regulatory breach reporting requirements. 6.10.1 Security incidents must be clearly defined and prioritized based on severity to ensure appropriate visibility and timely mitigation. These incidents may include, but are not limited to, exposure of confidential data, criminal activity or investigations, denial-of-service attacks, malicious code, policy violations, unauthorized monitoring, rogue services, spam sourcing, unauthorized access, unpatched vulnerabilities, web defacement, or false alerts. The Security Incident Response Policy outlines the procedures for identifying, managing, and resolving such incidents. 6.10.2 All mitigated major security related incidents need to be documented and reported to the appropriate senior management level. The incident escalation procedure ensures that management of incidents is based on priority and severity. Based on the criticality/severity of the security breach incident, Global IT will work with the Incident Response Team to communicate breach incident reports with regulatory bodies, as necessary.

Entegris should establish a comprehensive risk management program, that includes developing and publishing a Risk Management policy and standard. Entegris must also implement tools, where supported and feasible, to conduct effective risk management operations, including capturing of risks, impact assessments, mitigation, closure, risk monitoring and reporting. 6.11.1 Technology Supplier risk management​ Entegris should establish a comprehensive supplier risk management program, that includes developing and publishing a Supplier Risk Management policy and standard, and work processes to ensure all suppliers go through a preliminary vetting process, and then initial and periodic risk assessments conducted for all critical suppliers. Entegris must also ensure that any suppliers’ access to Entegris information systems and networks is controlled and provided following a technology review and approval process. Entegris must publish periodically critical supplier risk assessment reports for the review of Entegris ELT

Entegris shall establish and operationalize a comprehensive IT Governance structure and program to oversee governance activities and ensure the effective implementation of IT General Controls and other regulatory requirements. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) will be accountable for conducting periodic control assessments, identifying gaps, and managing remediation programs to address those gaps.

Entegris shall develop and implement a formal process to evaluate the cybersecurity implications of new and emerging technologies considered for adoption. This process will include risk assessments to identify potential threats posed by such technologies and provide guidance to business leaders on secure adoption strategies and mitigation of identified risks. Where necessary, Cybersecurity team shall update existing cybersecurity policies and/or develop and publish new policies to help adopt new technologies for use at Entegris.
documents.s: 6.13 Cybersecurity of new and emerging technologies

documents.t: It is essential that when traveling internationally on business purposes, all employees must follow Entegris International Travel Cybersecurity Guidelines and consider the destination country’s regulations and laws regarding technology being brought or imported. These steps are necessary to minimize Entegris data exposure, ensure regulatory compliance and to protect Entegris confidential and restricted data.

Entegris must develop an Exceptions Management policy and establish a procedure to manage exceptions. Exception must be submitted whenever any specific security policy requirement cannot be implemented or enforced due to technical or other operational reasons. All exceptions must be documented, risk assessed, approved, and periodically reported for the review of Cybersecurity Council and ELT

All security related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. Entegris IT Leadership will collaborate with Human Resources as needed to define appropriate content for new employee orientation, training and awareness. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies will be enforced through a combination of automated system or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

This policy provides guidance and make Entegris a risk managed organization by establishing requirements to develop a formal risk management program for identifying and managing cybersecurity risks associated with Entegris technology systems and components. The objectives of this policy are to: Ensure that all the current and future material cybersecurity related risks are identified, assessed, quantified, appropriately mitigated, and managed. Develop and implement a sustainable cybersecurity risk management framework, processes. Enable compliance with applicable regulations through the adoption of best practices. Minimize technology related risks to personnel safety, process safety and security of all Entegris personnel and operating facilities. Promote a pro-active approach in risk identification, reporting, evaluating, and resolving risks associated with the company’s operating asset.

This policy applies to all information and data assets, information resources and related infrastructure owned, managed, or administered by Entegris or owned and operated by a third-party on behalf of Entegris. This policy applies to anyone with access to Entegris information and information technology assets, including permanent, temporary, or contracted employees, consultants, or third-party organizations (henceforth referred to as the “users”). This policy applies to engineering, maintenance, operations, lab, Research and Development, information technology (IT), and business units directly involved in or related to plant manufacturing and operations. This policy is applicable to all Entegris Technology Systems, as defined in Section 4.0

This policy shall provide risk management guidance for the Entegris Technology Systems. This policy shall be supported by suitable Risk Management Standards, procedures, and tools. The risk management has three distinct phases: Risk Management, Risk Assessment, and Risk Mitigation

Entegris shall establish a comprehensive cyber risk management program, that includes developing and publishing Risk Management policy and standard, and work processes, to: 6.1.1 Identify – Develop an organizational understanding to manage cybersecurity risk to systems, people, assets, data, and capabilities. 6.1.2 Protect – Develop and implement appropriate safeguards to ensure delivery of critical services. 6.1.3 Detect – Develop and implement appropriate activities to identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity risk event. 6.1.4 Respond – Develop and implement appropriate activities to take action regarding a detected cybersecurity risk incident. 6.1.5 Recover – Develop and implement appropriate activities to maintain plans for resilience and to restore any capabilities or services that were impaired due to a cybersecurity incident. 6.1.6 Manage and mitigate risks from Suppliers and Third-parties or partners.
Entegris should also implement tools to conduct effective risk management activities, as given in sections 6.1.

6.3.1 Entegris should establish process to conduct risk impact assessments and then prioritize risks for further action. 6.3.2 Entegris shall use the Risk Matrix given below, as a guide to assess the impacts of a specific risk. 6.3.2.1 Risk Matrix​ Impact Area Low Medium High Critical Financial Limited/minor/ negligible financial impacts; < $ 500 K Medium impact/ Some significant impact; <$ 500K - 5 MM> High impact/ major financial impact; <$ 5 MM - 10 MM> Catastrophic impact; Financial impact: > $ 10MM++ Operational / Availability Disruption within one Unit Disruption in one or more sites Disruption leading to Service unavailability; stoppage of a manufacturing site Global impact, affecting all sites; complete manufacturing stoppage Regulatory Internal/ External observations; no fines External observations, with fines Regulatory assessment of non-compliance; no fines Regulatory non-compliance leading to imposition of fines Brand/ Reputation Internal concerns Local media news item State/ National news media story Global news media news Marketing/ Customer Internal concerns Customer/market retentions Customer communication on Audit Scores/ Negative commercial impact Significant loss of an order or total loss of contract 6.3.2.1 Business divisions must establish risk tolerance limits. With an understanding of risk tolerance, Business Divisions should prioritize cybersecurity activities, enabling business to make informed decisions about cybersecurity expenditures. 6.3.2.2 While aggregating all risks to Entegris overall risk posture, risk financial impacts should be calculated at Business Division level, applying weightage based on that business’s contributions to overall Entegris revenue.

6.4.1 Each Business Division shall designate person/s to manage their division’s cyber risk activities. 6.4.2 Each risk must have a designated Risk Owner, and the Risk Owner shall be responsible to arrange resources to mitigate the risks. 6.4.3 Entegris shall establish a central risk register and track all risks, and ensure all risks are addressed and responded to in a timely manner. All risks must be categorized, and aligned to business processes and sub-processes, as applicable. 6.4.4 Entegris shall establish process to periodically update Executive Leadership members on all critical and high risks.

6.5.1 All risks should be recorded in a central risk register and must be assigned a Risk Owner 6.5.2 Entegris shall establish process to assess risk impacts and initiate appropriate response based on risk severity, likelihood of occurrence, threat environments, and business conditions. The risk response options may include, to mitigate risk, transfer risk, or accept risk. 6.5.3 All risks in Risk Register shall be reviewed periodically for continued relevance, vis-à-vis changes in the business operational conditions or threat environment and re-assess the risk impacts and relevancy of the risk to the organization. The review frequency shall be determined based on risk level, but in any case, not more than one year. 6.5.4 Where it is decided to mitigate a risk, the mitigation progress must be tracked and reported until the mitigation is completed, and the risk no longer applicable. 6.5.5 Where Business division decides to accept a risk, an exception must be submitted, and shall be approved by the Business Leader

7.1.1 Entegris will develop role-based Cyber risks management training program for all the stakeholders involved in the risk management activities. 7.1.2 The training materials should be reviewed on periodic basis, and make necessary updates, and re-train the stakeholders.

It is expected that all Entegris technology teams will follow this policy requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business / Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented per Entegris Exception Management Process.

All cybersecurity related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. Entegris Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies must be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

1.1 The number and type of mobile devices entering the enterprise grows monthly, and the challenge for the IT security team gets ever more complex. The exploding number of devices significantly increases our risk to the different types of systems (with vulnerabilities) that authenticate to our network and transact data for business operations. This policy provides guidelines on how to meet the challenges that mobility brings into the enterprise. 1.2 The increased use of smartphones and tablets at Entegris requires IT to set controls on all those mobile endpoints. This policy provides an overview of controls that are deployed to protect these end points from being compromised and inappropriate use.
Endpoint devices can include PCs, laptops, smartphones and tablets globally.

IT provides the security configuration guidance to the end-user. With BYOD, every end user has the choice to enable the security configuration recommendations. All corporate devices will be managed globally by the IT team.
Reference Documents: 13823 - Enterprise System Password Standard Special Notes: Policy # DSS05.03.501
Term Definition Global Service Desk Entegris Help Desk Team MFA Multi-Factor Authentication SCCM Systems Center Configuration Manager

All mobile devices (laptops, tablets, iPads, smartphones, etc.) must have MFA enabled, and also mandate use of password, every time the device is powered-on/ restored from sleep mode to perform any functions. 6.1.1 All passwords should follow the Entegris password attributes as defined in the Enterprise Systems Password standard. 6.1.2 Users are encouraged to never share their passwords with co-workers/ friends to avoid potential inappropriate use. 6.1.3 The mobile device management software deployed on all smart phones and tablets that connect to Entegris internal data enforces the use of passwords. 6.1.4 Additional password protection controls Password used in automated logons (service accounts) must be encrypted. Transmission of passwords must be encrypted in transit. Passwords should not be stored in plain text on workstations or servers. Any password stored at rest must be encrypted. In the case where there is an indication of a possible system or password compromise, the password must be changed immediately.

Mobile devices running the iOS, Android, or Windows Mobile operating system will be installed with Microsoft Enterprise Mobility Management software. All Entegris company data and applications will be contained in the Microsoft Intune/ EMM container. Policy controls prevent integration between data in the Intune App and data elsewhere on the device. This applies to all smart phones and tablets, whether those are company provided or personal devices (BYOD).

6.3.1 All computers (clients and servers) connected physically or remotely to the Entegris network shall have antivirus software correctly installed, configured, activated, and updated with the latest version of virus definitions before or immediately upon connecting to the network. 6.3.2 If deemed necessary to prevent viral propagation to other networked devices or harmful effects to the network, computers infected with viruses, worms or other forms of malicious code (collectively referred to as "virus" or "viruses") shall be disconnected from the network until the infection has been removed. Entegris IT will install the standard Anti-virus software on all company computers. This software performs a weekly full scan of the hard drive to check for infection. The virus definition is updated real time, dynamically by the antivirus software vendor. 6.3.3 When an enterprise-wide virus attack is in progress, Entegris IT shall notify the computing community via the best available method, and all files on all hard drives should be scanned (automatically) immediately using the newest virus definitions available.

6.4.1 All Windows laptop computers are configured with the default Windows Bit-Locker encryption. This feature allows for data to be secure if the device is lost/ stolen and somebody attempts to compromise data from the internal hard-drive. 6.4.2 All data on Smart Phones and tablets that are encapsulated in the mobile device management (MDM) application is encrypted on the mobile device by the application. Deleting the application deletes all data that is associated with the application.

During regular business operations, Entegris IT support may need control over the employee’s PC to assist in configurations, bug fixing, etc. All PCs are installed with necessary software (utilize screen-share feature) to enable IT Support Team to connect remotely to the employee’s PC, to perform maintenance activities. Employees are expected to never tamper with the configuration settings of the software application.

Only Entegris certified approved applications can be installed on Entegris deployed PCs. All users don’t have administrator rights to their laptops and will need both appropriate manager approvals and assistance from Entegris IT Support Team to install non-standard applications. Updates to installed applications will require assistance from the IT Support Team to minimize down-stream installation and configuration problems.

The Entegris Service Desk team manages the roll-out of Microsoft patches on a periodic basis using a centralized Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) application, and also other cloud-based applications. Based on vendor releases, patches are evaluated and deployed to all Windows computers. Logging onto the Entegris network is needed to download and apply the patches. As some patches require system reboots, it is recommended to reboot all PCs every 2 weeks.

Local admin rights have been disabled on all enterprise PCs. PCs that require tooling and service engineers to install and test codes/ programs are managed as exceptions. No user is to tamper with these settings on any enterprise provided end point.

This policy defines the requirements and criteria for seeking exceptions to any Entegris information technology, operational technology, digital assets related architectural and cybersecurity controls, essential to protect Entegris Information and Data assets, and for securing Entegris operations. This policy: ensures that all control exceptions are risk assessed, approved, recorded, tracked, and reported helps businesses to focus on control gaps and address them prioritized based on risk severity Helps keep track of exceptions taken and overall risk posture Reduces overall risk, by reducing number of controls exceptions over a period

This Exception Policy is applicable to all IT and OT security and architectural controls as documented in various policies and standards that are applicable to information and data assets, operational technology assets. Term Definition Application A software program hosted by an information system. Control The safeguards or countermeasures prescribed for an information system or an organization to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the system and its information. Risk Risk: a function of the threats, assets, controls and impact factors (e.g., laws, etc.) that drive loss exposure. A risk is a measure of the extent to which Entegris is threatened by a potential circumstance or event and is a function of: the adverse impacts that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs. Risk Assessment The process of identifying risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, resulting from the operation of a system. Risk management includes threat and vulnerability analyses as well as analyses of adverse effects on individuals arising from information processing and considers mitigations provided by security and privacy controls planned or in place. Synonymous with risk analysis Information System A discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information
