Entegris technology leadership must establish an Exception Management policy, and procedures, and tools for submitting technology exceptions for review, approval, and tracking Establish process for identifying control gaps and determine where controls exceptions are required. (Refer to Figure #1 Exception Management Process)

In general, exceptions maybe considered under the following situations: The Business needs time to implement the required control and agreeing to complete the implementation within the exception period. The system/application under consideration is due for retirement or will be replaced within 6 – 12 months period A required control cannot be implemented due to technical limitations within the system/application Other unique business situations and/or operational conditions prevent Business to implement required security controls NOTE: For all these above situations, it is expected that alternative mitigating controls will be implemented during the exception period or till the control requirements are met.

All exception requests must be submitted, following process flow depicted in figure #1, and described in this and other sections of this policy. Exception requirements shall be determined based on the control gaps identified, per section 6.4 Control Gaps Identification and Risk Assessment, given below. All exception requests must be submitted, following the steps given in section 6.5 Any exception should be given for a maximum period of 1 year. If further extension required, then a new exception request must be initiated and approved, per the process. All Exceptions must be documented, tracked, periodically reviewed for gap remediation progress and/or continued relevance and risk, and must eventually be closed. This Exception Lifecycle Management should generally follow the process, given in Figure #1, below: The source document presents a Figure #1 Exception Management Process flow diagram here.

As Cyber threats keep increasing and cyber-attacks are getting more sophisticated, it is imperative that additional security controls will be needed to protect Entegris data on its applications and systems. Also, Entegris may need to update its control policies due to change in applicable regulations or sometime due to specific requirements from our customer agreements. All these factors require Entegris to update its current cybersecurity policies or create new policies and standard, to enforce additional controls in its technology environment. At Entegris, exception process starts upon identifying control gaps, based on specific control requirements applicable to a particular application or system. Control gap identification will be done per the guidance given below: 6.4.1 New applications and/or systems​ All new applications and/or systems will be subjected to Technology Review Board (TRB) and Architectural Review Board (ARB) review processes, and as part of this review, all required control will be identified based on the type of data the application/system is expected to collect, process, store, or transfer. Based on this analysis, if any control gaps are anticipated, an exception request must be initiated, prior to the production launch of the application/system. All exception requests must meet the Exceptions Criteria given in section 6.2, above. 6.4.2 Existing applications and/or systems​ Existing application / systems may need an exception, due to release of new or updated Entegris policies or due to identification of control gaps through audits or other risk assessment processes. Whenever a new control policy issued or an existing policy is updated, or a control gap is identified, the application and/or system owner should conduct a gap analysis to confirm whether the application/systems meet the new control requirements or not. Where necessary, then an exception would be considered. All exception requests must meet the Exceptions Criteria given in section 6.2, above.
documents.s: 6.4 Control gaps identification and Risk Assessment

documents.t: Exception requests must be submitted through a formal process by the concerned business/technology lead. All exception requests must go through a risk review process and risk assessed Exception request shall also be reviewed by the concerned Policy Owner (the policy controls against which the exception is sought), work with the business/technology leads to conduct exception risk analysis and appraise the business /Technology VP on the potential risk to Entegris. The Policy Owner may suggest alternative methods to meet the control intent, instead of seeking an exception. Every exception request must clearly state the justification for seeking the exception, and what compensating controls are in place to reduce the risk to Entegris, during the period of exception. All exception requests shall be approved by respective Technology VP and Business VP, acknowledging the risk associated with that specific exception The Policy Owner may escalate the exception request to the Cybersecurity Council, if the exception request is not meeting the exception request criterion.

All approved exceptions shall be valid for a maximum period of 12 months ONLY. The validity also depends upon the effectiveness of the counter measures implemented. The Business shall take appropriate actions to fix the control gaps within the given exception period Exception should be re-assessed prior to completion of exception validity period Where necessary, a new exception request must be submitted prior to the expiration of initial approval, and must again go through risk review & risk assessment, and approval process

Cybersecurity Policies and Risk Manager shall be responsible for establishing a process to record and track all exception requests, and their disposition Exceptions approved and the resulting risk to Entegris must be documented and reported to the ELT on a periodic basis Exceptions trends should be tracked, and suitable strategy shall be recommended to increase compliance and limit number of exceptions.

It is expected that all information technology and operational technology teams in Entegris will follow this policy requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business/Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented per Entegris Exception Management Process.

All security related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. IT and OT Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies will be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

documents.t: The purpose of this policy is to dictate the process for appropriately authorizing, documenting, and controlling access / security privileges to Entegris’ information, software, and systems. The objectives of this policy are to: Establish requirements to manage user access and prevent unauthorized access to Entegris information and information assets, systems, and applications. Establish requirements for network access management, including remote and wireless access. Establish and define user responsibilities for protecting authentication information. 1.1 This policy defines requirements for ensuring access to Entegris technology systems, applications, information data assets, and infrastructure components are granted based on the concepts of: a. Least privilege b. Business need c. Role-based access d. Prevention of unauthorized access

2.1 The scope of the policy is global, covering access management requirements for all Entegris Technology systems, (including IT and OT servers, databases, applications, network infrastructure, and all components related to OT Manufacturing systems [PLCs, Networks, CNC, etc.]), and all Entegris information assets. 2.2 This policy applies to all technologies and information assets regardless of ownership or management; whether managed or administered by Entegris or owned and/or operated by a third-party on behalf of Entegris. This policy is applicable to all business and production facilities across the globe. 2.3 This policy is applicable to all Entegris Employees, Contractors, Consultants 3rd party service providers, and Entegris Customers that need to access Entegris technology systems.

Business Sponsor/ Leader Responsible to approve access requests coming from their divisions Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) Ensure Access Management program is operational and effective Follows-up with Business Leaders to ensure Access management process is followed and unauthorized access is not restricted. Communicate access management risks and overall effectiveness of access management program to executive leadership Responsible for developing access management control practices, and guiding technology teams in implementing identity and access management controls and operationalizing them. Establish process to communicate policy non-compliance instances to the relevant asset owners, and monitor & report on remediation status, Cybersecurity Council The Cyber Security Council is a cross-functional technology and business leadership forum responsible to: Ensure that the technology teams are working on appropriately prioritized security initiatives and in line with business requirements. Assign adequate resources for successful operation of access management program System Owner and Application Owners Responsible to ensure the system/s and/or applications they own are meeting the requirements of this policy, and related standards. Person or organization responsible for the development, procurement, integration, modification, operation and maintenance, and/or final disposition of an information system, and ensure. Infrastructure, Network & Operations team Establish required access provisioning and deprovisioning processes, tools and manage operations

Term Definition Access control The process of granting or denying specific requests for obtaining and using information and related information processing services; and to enter specific physical facilities (e.g., Federal buildings, military establishments, and border crossing entrances). Authenticator Something that the claimant possesses and controls (typically a cryptographic module or password) that is used to authenticate the claimant’s identity. This was previously referred to as a token. Authorization Access privileges granted to a user, program, or process or the act of granting those privileges. Least privilege (principle of) The principle that a security architecture is designed so that each entity is granted the minimum system resources and authorizations that the entity needs to perform its function. Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) An authentication system or an authenticator that requires more than one authentication factor for successful authentication. Multi-factor authentication can be performed using a single authenticator that provides more than one factor or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are. See authenticator. Network Access Access to a system by a user (or a process acting on behalf of a user) communicating through a network, including a local area network, a wide area network, and the Internet Privileged Users A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform. Role-based Access Control (RBAC) Access control based on user roles (i.e., a collection of access authorizations that a user receives based on an explicit or implicit assumption of a given role). Role permissions may be inherited through a role hierarchy and typically reflect the permissions needed to perform defined functions within an organization. A given role may apply to a single individual or to several individuals Service Accounts Specialized non-human privileged accounts typically used within operating systems to execute applications or other services so they can access data and network resources to perform specific tasks. User Individual, or (system) process acting on behalf of an individual, authorized to access a system. User Account types Employee: Users directly hired by Entegris, either as full-time or part-time employees. Contractor/Consultant: Users who are not Entegris employees, but are hired through third party companies or as independent service providers, for short-term resources augmentation to meet business needs. Third Party users: Typically, Entegris partners or Customers, who may be given access to Entegris systems, for specific activities related to their engagement. Segregation of Duties (SoD) The concept of having more than one person required to complete a task. It is an administrative control used by organizations to prevent fraud, sabotage, theft, misuse of information, and other security compromises.

6.1.1 All user accounts to access Entegris systems must be granted through a formal documented approval process. All user access approvals shall conform to segregation of duties requirements. 6.1.2 All the Third-party, Customer, and contractor resource access-accounts shall be requested/approved by the concerned Entegris Business Sponsor, and access shall be given only on as-needed basis with least privileges and must be revoked as soon as the access is no longer required. 6.1.3 All user access must be revoked immediately upon termination of employment or completion of contact engagement. 6.1.3.1 User access to specific Entegris systems or applications shall be disabled, if the user is no longer required to have that access, either due to job transfer, change of role/ responsibilities, extended leave (if applicable) and at the request of competent authority (Security Operations, CISO, CIO or executive management). 6.1.3.2 All user access must be logged, and access logs must be audited on a periodic basis to confirm that granting access and revocation is performed in accordance with this policy and applicable standards.

6.2.1 Entegris must ensure that all physical access to its information systems, operational technology assets, other digital assets, and access to facilities containing physical assets are controlled and authorized. 6.2.2 All physical access events are logged, and records maintained. 6.2.3 Users must be responsible for protecting Entegris equipment and data in accordance with Entegris policy when left unattended within the Entegris facility or at an off-site location.
6.3.1 Entegris must establish a Remote Access Management standard that includes remote access control requirements and process to request and grant remote access to the users.

6.4.1 Entegris shall establish process, tools, and resources to ensure access permissions and authorizations are managed, incorporating the principles of least privilege, and account for separation of duties as required.

6.5.1 Unique Identity​ 6.5.1.1 Entegris must ensure that all its Users are assigned a unique identifier (User ID), and their access is controlled through a combination of User ID and password combination. 6.5.1.2 Entegris must establish a standard format for creating userIDs. 6.5.2 Passwords​ Entegris shall maintain a password standard that provides guidelines for users to create passwords to use on Entegris systems and will review that standard on a regular basis. 6.5.2.1 Passwords for unique User IDs shall not be shared in any form except as noted below: 6.5.2.1.1 During the initial User Provisioning process, the first password for a new employee is shared by the IT provisioning team, with the manager, and to the employee to enable their access. All new employees will be forced to change the password at the first login.
documents.s: 6.5 Identities are proofed and bound to credentials and asserted in interactions

documents.t: Shared accounts are to be eliminated, wherever possible. Where shared accounts are required, then the following controls shall be implemented to limit the access of the User IDs: 6.6.1 Shared accounts are to be isolated to specific machines and must not be domain-level accounts. 6.6.2 Shared account passwords must be changed periodically, at least once annually.

6.7.1 All users must be authenticated, prior to allowing access to any Entegris technology resource. 6.7.2 For all high-risk resource access, multi-factor authentication (MFA) techniques must be deployed. 6.7.3 Where technically feasible, user sessions will timeout after extended periods of inactivity and users must reauthenticate to resume access.
documents.s: 6.7 Authenticate Users, devices, and other assets

documents.t: 6.8.1 Each service account must have an account owner. 6.8.2 Static Service accounts are to be avoided. Applications that only support static Service Accounts will require manual procedures to rotate the password. 6.8.3 Service Accounts must be named per a standard so they are identifiable in audit logs and can be incorporated into rules for alerting.

6.9.1 Entegris shall incorporate the principle of least functionality by configuring systems to provide only essential capabilities. 6.9.2 All privileged user roles and functions shall be defined and documented, and all privileged users are listed, and their access logs are captured. Privileged user access logs must be reviewed on a periodic basis, for anomalies.
6.10.1 Entegris must establish controls to prevent repeated failed in logins.

6.11.1 All User access events shall be logged, and records maintained for audit purposes. 6.11.2 User accounts and access privileges must be reviewed on a periodic basis, and any anomalies must be addressed.

It is expected that all Entegris technology will follow this policy requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business/Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented per Entegris Exception Management Process.

All cybersecurity related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. Entegris Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers, Third parties, Customers, and contractors who will be accessing Entegris Technology systems shall be required to abide by this identity and access management policy.

All security related policies must be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

It is essential that when traveling internationally on business purposes, particularly traveling to high-risk countries, all employees must consider the following guidelines to minimize data exposure and to protect Entegris confidential data: Leave regular corporate devices back at home or office and obtain a loaner device. Loaner devices shall have only limited number of applications and no data stored in local drives, and with USB ports disabled. To the extent possible, access company email only through webmail. To the extent possible, access all required applications for work through cloud. Company portal application (Microsoft Intune) must be uninstalled from the mobile phone or iPad/tablets, prior to the destination country, so that no Entegris data can be accessed or downloaded to the phone. Do not download any email attachment to the loaner device. USB access should be disabled for all non-Entegris approved USB devices. Do not use wi-fi networks available in public places, such as, airports or coffee shops and restaurants.

To protect Entegris proprietary information, intellectual property, and other sensitive / confidential data all employees traveling internationally where data encrypted devices are not permitted (or subject to forfeiture. Etc,.) for business purposes, must use a loaner device (laptop) which should be using during the duration of their travel. This will also help Entegris meet country specific regulations on device encryptions, and protect Entegris data. Who should be requesting for a Loaner laptop? Any Entegris employees or contractors traveling internationally from the home-office to other countries for business purposes, where data encrypted devices are not permitted How to get a Loaner device? You should submit a request for loaner device, at least 1 week, prior to the date of travel Loaner Device request must be submitted through ServiceNow NOTE: All Loaner devices must be returned to the location, where it is issued from.

Provide guidelines on how to respond in the event of an incident and avoid being trapped in fire-fighting mode. 1.1 Technology related Cyber incidents can threaten the productivity of the business. IT must establish a consistent set of criteria to determine what is considered an incident and ensure that appropriate guidelines and resources are available to address such issues when they arise. 1.2 Pre-planning the response actions allows for providing a heads-up for all teams involved. Everyone has an important part to play in reporting incidents in order to mitigate consequences and reduce the risk of similar repeating incidents.
2.1 All types of un-planned incidents which affect any system or application that is used to support business processes. 2.2 Major disasters are to be addressed in the Disaster Recovery Plans.

3.1 Incident Response roles and responsibilities need to be defined by the Incident Leader at the time of the incident. Guidelines on response procedures are developed with all critical business functions. The incident leader should ensure that appropriate functional points of contact are engaged in the event of any incident that could potentially impact critical business operations.
Reference Documents: None listed. Special Notes: Policy # DSS02.05.501

Term Definition Incident An event that causes a significant business disruption/inconvenience. Based on the impact to business operations, they could vary from localized site (all teams at a site are unable to access critical applications) to global outages (critical applications are unavailable for all end users) for significant time periods (>30 min). Cyber Incident An event occurring on or conducted through a computer network that actually or imminently jeopardizes the integrity, confidentiality, or availability of computers, information or communications systems or networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by computers or information systems, or information resident thereon. Significant Cyber Incident A cyber incident that is (or group of related cyber incidents that together are) likely to result in demonstrable harm to the national security interests, foreign relations, or economy of the United States or to the public confidence, civil liberties, or public health and safety of any Entegris employee. Major Disaster Disaster has crippled multiple critical operations on-site. Access to the site could be very limited and multiple critical systems and applications are in-accessible. Causes for such disasters could range from Geophysical (Earthquake, Volcanic, Landslide, Rockfall, Avalanche, etc.), Hydrological (Storm Surge, Coastal Flood, Local Floods, etc.), Meteorological (Tropical Cyclone, Local Storm, etc.), Climatological (Heat Wave, Cold Wave, Extreme Winter, Forest Fire, etc.), Biological (Viral, bacterial, fungal) or Man Made (Terrorist Attack, Chemical Spills or Infrastructure — Transport and Utilities) related. RCA Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is a document that investigates details about the incident.

6.1 This policy provides a framework for reporting and handling of incidents that can threaten the productivity of the business — e.g. the impacts could encompass the loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability of key systems, impacts to privacy as well as potential impacts to safety where operational technology is in scope. 6.1.1 Technology related incidents could be broadly classified as: Service Degradation / Minor Outages Cyber-Security Incidents Major Outages (addressed by Disaster Recovery Plan) 6.2 Invariable of the classification, all incidents should be reported to the Entegris Helpdesk (1-800 889 8166 / 1-952 556 4357, entegris.help.desk@entegris.com, or https://entegris.cherwellondemand.com/CherwellPortal/IT). The helpdesk team should log the incident in the ITSM application appropriately to track it to closure. 6.3 The helpdesk should work with appropriate IT Management to define: a. Overall Incident Manager b. Designate IT Director (by affected Domain) The Incident Manager will manage all engagements related to support needed by both internal and external (providers, partners, etc.) teams to manage the incident effectively. 6.4 Going forward the Incident Manager and IT Director need to manage all components of the incident:

Analysis includes: Incident Detection Scope of Incident Business Impact Analysis, etc. Including additional IT and Business Team Members 6.4.1.1 Focus on managing the consequences – not the causes – of the incident. 6.4.1.2 Once an incident happens, focus on the core of the incident to define your investigation and response. This analysis will make it possible for the enterprise to respond effectively and appropriately to an incident, and to minimize the damage from it. The root cause of the incident (that is, the vulnerability that allowed it to happen) can be analyzed and managed once the initial analysis is completed.

Communication includes: Immediate Internal / External Long-term and On-going 6.4.2.1 Crisis communication procedures, including well-crafted messages, are vital to ensuring that the organization maintains control of the situation to keep fear, uncertainty and rumors at a minimum. Addressing the expectations for all stakeholders of the organization is vital for the effective management of communications during an incident.

Resolution/Closure includes: Quick / Immediate fix Short-term (CIP) Long-term (road-map) 6.4.3.1 A main purpose of an Incident Response Program is to ensure efficient recovery through the effective mitigation of vulnerabilities and the reinstatement of repaired systems. Recovery includes ensuring that vulnerabilities should be addressed enterprise-wide and further exploitation of similar vulnerabilities should be minimized. Based on the scope, mitigations could be classified in either of the listed categories.

Based on the above components, the Incident Manager and the IT Director need to assess if an RCA is necessary and ensure that appropriate documentation is completed if deemed necessary. All critical incidents — like those that result in the potential loss of intellectual property or compromise privacy matters — should have an RCA completed. The RCA should be leveraged by the helpdesk/other support teams as a learning to address similar incidents in the future. 6.4.5 All Cyber-security Incidents will include a mandatory RCA process that documents incident details and mitigations implemented to resolve the same. In addition, if necessary, the IT Management Team will communicate the same to appropriate Business Leadership/external compliance authorities.

In extreme circumstances where persistent cyber threats have the ability to cripple critical business applications and systems, the IT team can disable all connectivity between the Internal Entegris Corporate Network and the External Internet.

It is the responsibility of Entegris authorized individuals to report any breach instances to the appropriate Data Protection Authority within 72 hrs. of detecting the breach. 6.7 Process flows in Appendix A, B and D define the schematic flow of events to address the different types of incidents.

documents.t: An investigation/integrated response to security incidents requires disciplined coordination of multiple moving parts both at the strategic (governance) and tactical (process) levels. Based on the incident impact, the Director — Security, Risk & Compliance will be responsible to conduct appropriate investigations. During the course of investigation, certain actions that otherwise may be called policy violations (collecting evidence — forensics by design, focused monitoring, log analysis, etc.) could be required.

For significant security incidents, there could be a need to include additional teams and members to handle and manage the business impacts. The Director — Security, Risk and Compliance will lead this CSIRT group that could include members from IT, Legal, HR, Marketing/Communications, Internal Audit and Business Line Managers. Not all members will be involved in all incidents, but all members must be pre-defined, informed of their responsibilities, trained and made to participate in regular training events. When engaged, the CSIRT will have the ability to assert authority and get support from all needed teams to effectively manage the incident and its impacts.

Company-wide Internal and External communications will be handled by the IT Servicedesk and MARCOM organizations. The legal counsel should be involved (to review content and engagement schedule) in communications with external law enforcement groups (FBI, Secret Service, DHS, etc.).

Determining the components of a successful incident response plan will vary from business to business, but at its core should deliver the following: An executive commitment and endorsement of the incident response initiative A Cyber Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) comprised of members with varying areas of expertise ranging from IT to legal and communications A defined communication plan A plan to support, maintain and test the incident response plan on a regular basis An organized, structured approach that clearly defines the roles and responsibilities for all parties involved A clearly stated definition of what an incident means to your organization and how incident response aligns with existing organizational security efforts, such as business continuity and disaster recovery plans A well-defined plan on how to monitor and analyze potential threats to the environment An operation plan that defines how incidents are declared and initial steps for information gathering A post-incident process for lessons learned and process improvement A successful incident response program should align with standards set forth by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL).

Stage 1: Establish Incident — This is the stage where the incident is detected and logged. This stage is crucial to ensure response actions are known and coordinated. Good preparations will help us limit the potential damage by ensuring quick and effective response actions. Processes involved would include: Define CSIRT team members — individuals that will be involved with managing the incident; the right people with the appropriate skill set. Define the criteria to declare an incident. Events, alerts, incidents (managed) and incidents (un-managed)/crisis should be appropriately classified to ensure appropriate responses. Define communication protocols needed to manage the incident. Define documentation overheads needed to manage and report the incident. Define a general direction for response action plans. Stage 2: Identification — This is the stage where we declare if an incident has occurred. Based on events observation and indicators, we look for deviations from normal operations. We look for malicious acts or attempts to do harm. The security mechanism in place will help us with the identification. The IT Infrastructure team will use their experience to look at the signs and indicators. The observation could occur at network level, host level or system level. It's where we leverage the alerts and logs from our routers, firewalls, IDS, AV gateways, operating system, network flows, etc. Processes involved would include: After identifying an incident we need to assess the scope, magnitude and impact. Notify the appropriate individuals (add to CSIRT members) or external parties. If there are reasons to believe that we will engage law enforcement, it's where we ensure chain of custody. Define next steps such as containment. Stage 3: Containment — This stage involves limiting the damage. Stop the bleeding. Stop the attacker. Depending on the scope, magnitude and impact of the incident, processes involved would include: Make the decision on which strategy we use to contain the incident based on our processes and procedures. Engage the business owners and decide to shut down the system or disconnect the network or continue operations and monitor the activity. Stage 4: Eradication — After successfully containing the incident, this stage entails removing the cause of the incident. In the case of a virus incident it may simply require removing the virus. In other complex incident cases we might need to identify and mitigate exploited vulnerabilities. Processes involved would include: Determine how the risk exploited an existing vulnerability. Apply the necessary measures to ensure it does not happen again. Ensure that all analysis is appropriately documented for all future reference. Stage 5: Recovery — This stage means back in production. Eventually, restoring a backup or re-imaging a system. It's where we return to normal operational status. After successful restoration it is important to monitor the target for a certain time period to potentially identify signs that evaded detection. Stage 6: Lessons Learned — Follow up activity is crucial. Processes involved would include: Root Cause Analysis document to reflect and document what happened. We can learn what failed and what worked. Identify improvements for your incident handling processes and procedures. Document and complete final report.

documents.t: Reporting to all external and third parties where applicable. Who needs incident response? In short: everyone. All BUs have intellectual property, personally identifiable information (PII), financials or some form of sensitive information that can be dangerous when in the wrong hands. Establishing an actionable plan will result in faster response times and minimize damages as a result of an incident. The potential risks that Entegris faces as the result of poorly responding to an incident could vary. That said, below are some of the more common risks to consider when evaluating the value of Entegris' incident response plan: Operational risks: An incident such as a system breach could result in critical systems and applications becoming inoperative. This may lead to a loss of core business functions (such as a production line being shut down) as well as potential security vulnerabilities. Reputational risks: Responding poorly to an incident can have severely negative impacts on your organization's public image, as well as in the eyes of your current and potential customers/clients. Compliance risks: In some instances, an incident may result in an inability to meet regulatory requirements and introduces the potential for fines and/or penalties from governing bodies. Financial risks: All the previously mentioned risks have the potential to result in negative financial impact to your organization. These, along with the potential for lost assets, the cost of repairs, legal fees and other unexpected costs, should be considered.

Actual incident details and timeline: "WannaCry" Ransomware spread globally between 12th–15th May 2017. The first initial US-CERT Alert was released on May 12th, but a second detailed alert was received on Saturday, May 13, 2017 11:13 AM EDT. The first Microsoft Alert was received on Saturday, May 13, 2017 3:26 AM EDT. On the basis of the Microsoft alert, GBKhor completed the mitigation work in the Anti-virus and Firewall applications and notified the global infrastructure team on published data and plans. RBlount led the communications by notifying specific individuals — IT Management and Infrastructure team members — on detailed next steps and plans on Sat 5/13/2017 2:34 PM EDT. JSantos, GSigwanz, AKlaus and GBKhor were all engaged and executed mitigation actions to minimize ransomware impact. The first InfraGard Alert was received on Saturday, May 13, 2017 3:24 PM EDT. RBlount led the formal communications on Sun 5/14/2017 8:24 AM EDT notifying the IT Management and Global Infrastructure teams on Entegris readiness. Enterprise-wide communication on Ensider was posted on Sun 5/14/2017 11:11 AM EDT. Enterprise-wide communication from the Helpdesk was posted on Sun 5/14/2017 12:13 PM EDT. Enterprise-wide communication of appropriate mitigations and success was communicated on yammer. Microsoft released patches for this vulnerability in March and April to address servers and workstations respectively. 85% of our internal systems were compliant prior to the outbreak. This stresses the importance of timely patching. Result: Successful Mitigation — No significant impact to business operations, teams and sites due to the ransomware and its variants. Lessons Learned: Probability of success for such incidents (immediate pro-active mitigation work) is greatly increased by engaging the right people within the IT organization as early as possible. In addition to operational level-debugging and fixes, communications should be appropriately managed both at the execution team and enterprise levels. Possible addition: Informing all IT Directors to make them aware that IT Infrastructure is working on the issue and can address any concerns. Possible addition: CIO communication to ELT/Greg.

documents.t: This document describes the universal process. It is the Entegris Way. This policy deals with managing Supplier cybersecurity risks associated with Entegris' suppliers, vendors, or other entities (collectively referred to as Suppliers) who provide materials, services, or products for Entegris to manage its product development, manufacturing, information systems, and operations. This policy is essential because Entegris operations depend on these Suppliers, which allows us to succeed in the marketplace. To be successful, Entegris must ensure that all the risks associated with these Suppliers are assessed and mitigated. Entegris must ensure that each Supplier is operating with industry standard engineering and cybersecurity practices so that Entegris can be more secure and operate our business with greater reliability. Entegris may also need to demonstrate to our customers that Entegris has Supplier risk management practices in line with industry standards, which in turn help boost confidence in our operations management. Managing Supplier risks essential for certain contract conditions, or for complying with regulatory requirements.

2.1 This policy is intended to cover the people, processes, and technologies used in an effective supplier management operational strategy, and is applicable to all Entegris personnel, such as, Sourcing and Procurement team members, Business Sponsors, Cyber Security team, Enterprise Architecture and security architecture teams, Supplier Risk Managers, Quality teams and other people who will be involved in engaging and managing suppliers for various services and/or delivery of products to support Entegris Technology systems and operations. 2.2 This policy applies globally to all Entegris sites, where Suppliers are engaged for delivering services, materials, and products. 2.3 Out of scope: Entegris Customers with access to our systems or data.

The following is a list of stakeholders and their responsibilities for implementing and operating this policy. Accountable (A) / Responsible (R) is noted for each role. Business Sponsor — Accountable (A) Ensure supplier onboarding has followed policy needs and owns mitigation actions for known defects Support the supplier evaluation process Responsible for mitigating all risks related to their suppliers Provide business justification for suppliers who do not meet required risk posture Chief Information Security Officer — Accountable (A) Ensure Supplier Risk Management program is operational Follow-up with Business Leaders to ensure Supplier risks are mitigated in a timely manner Communicate Supplier risks and overall supplier risk posture to Executive Leadership Sourcing / Procurement Managers — Responsible (R) Act as Entegris Point of Contact and liaison between the Business Sponsor, Supplier Risk Manager, Legal and other stakeholders, and with the potential suppliers Manage the RFP process and short-list potential suppliers Responsible to verify and ensure that a potential Supplier has good reputation and doing business with them will not impact reputation of Entegris Work with Business Sponsor to understand business needs and help negotiate the contract Cybersecurity Supplier Risk Manager (Cybersecurity Team) — Responsible (R) Work with Business Sponsors, manage Supplier Risk Assessment activities, and follow-up on compliance gaps and ensuring gaps are closed or mitigated Report on Supplier risk profiles, and overall Entegris Supplier Risk posture and compliance metrics Plan periodic risk re-assessments of the identified Suppliers Enterprise Architecture — Responsible (R) Perform supplier assessment and architectural review for all technology suppliers' solutions identified

Term Definition Information Systems A discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information. Risk Assessment The process of identifying risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, resulting from the operation of a system. Risk Mitigation Prioritizing, evaluating, and implementing the appropriate risk reducing controls / countermeasures recommended from the risk management process. Risk Ranking The process of classifying risks based on the expected impact to the organization. Supplier Organization or individual that enters into an agreement with Entegris or its authorized entities for the supply of a product or service. This includes all suppliers in the supply chain, developers or manufacturers of systems, system components, or system services; systems integrators; suppliers; product resellers; and third-party partners. The terms 3rd Party or Vendor or 3rd Party Service Provider or Managed Service Provider are also used interchangeably as Supplier, within Entegris environment. Request for Proposal (RFP) Request for Proposal – a detailed specification of goods or services required by Entegris, sent to potential suppliers, for them to respond with their proposal.

6.1 Entegris must ensure that each Supplier is operating with good engineering and cybersecurity practices so that Entegris can be more secure and operate our business with greater reliability. 6.1.1 All Suppliers shall be risk assessed prior to on-boarding. 6.1.2 Business Sponsor must work with suppliers to close known prioritized gaps identified in evaluation in a timely manner and provide justification to Sourcing where suppliers do not meet right posture. 6.1.3 Supplier risk management roles and responsibilities related to supplier management activities shall be defined. 6.1.4 For all technology suppliers, Entegris should verify that the solution offered by the Supplier meets Entegris Architecture and secure architecture requirements, and the solution is supportable with people with appropriate skills, and other resources necessary to operate and maintain the solution. 6.1.4.1 Entegris Enterprise Architecture team must ensure all technology suppliers and their solution use has gone through a review process. 6.1.5 Suppliers providing direct support of Entegris systems and devices must have a Master Services Agreement in place. Access to Entegris networks and systems must not be granted unless such an agreement exists.

Entegris should use multiple risk factors to identify a given Supplier's impact to the organization. Based on this assessment, Entegris shall classify its suppliers, as given below: 6.2.1 Tier 1 Supplier — These are business defined suppliers that pertain critical risk in providing business services. These should be defined by the sourcing organization. 6.2.2 High Risk Supplier — These include Tier 1 suppliers identified by sourcing and any additional High-Risk suppliers that business sponsor may identify as critical. 6.2.2.1 For IT and digital purposes, High-Risk suppliers include the following. Suppliers with - Privileged administrative access for a High-Risk system or application Access to confidential / restricted data Access to proprietary source code Remote access to any Entegris devices 6.2.3 Non-Critical Supplier — All suppliers that are not Tier 1 or High-Risk category will be considered as non-critical Suppliers.

Managing Supplier risks essential for certain contract conditions, or for complying with regulatory requirements. 6.3.1 Supplier contracts must include requirements related to secure business practices to be followed by the Supplier. 6.3.2 All Suppliers shall be classified into either Tier 1, High Risk or Non-critical suppliers, based on the products/services they provide to Entegris, and their potential impact on Entegris in the event of performance failure by the Supplier. 6.3.3 Tier 1 / High Risk Suppliers shall be periodically risk assessed, and corrective measures shall be taken, if any required, to mitigate identified risks. 6.3.4 All new and renewed Supplier contracts shall include a clause that, "Entegris (or its authorized agents) can gain access to Supplier's systems/documents, and facilities to conduct on-site audits, or virtual or online assessments, if necessary." 6.3.5 Entegris shall document its risk analysis of Suppliers and maintain the records.

Entegris will notify its customers, in accordance with applicable regulations or contract requirements, should an adverse cyber event occur at one of our suppliers that will impact production or delivery of goods to the customer.

6.5.1 Suppliers must be on Entegris' Qualified Supplier List. 6.5.2 Cybersecurity risks due to suppliers and other dependencies must be identified and addressed. 6.5.3 Supplier systems, assets, and software must be in compliance with the applicable Entegris policies, standards, and procedures. 6.5.4 The asset inventory, system architecture, access control, and vulnerability status of all third party owned / leased systems must be delivered and maintained by the supplier. Suppliers must maintain a security posture and comply with Entegris requirements throughout the engagement lifecycle. 6.5.5 Confidentiality agreements must be in place and up to date to comply with Entegris third party requirements. 6.5.6 All systems and software procured by supplier for use at Entegris must be approved through a change management process. 6.5.7 Supplier systems and software must be periodically reviewed. 6.5.8 When adding new software, only supplier-supported software shall be used (or approved open-source software). 6.5.9 New supplier software shall be added to Entegris software inventory.

It is expected that all Entegris technology teams will follow this policy requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business / Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented per Entegris Exception Management Process.

All cybersecurity related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. Entegris Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies must be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

This policy defines the requirements for Entegris' vulnerability and patch management program. The purpose of this policy is to formalize the process by which Entegris manages its existing and newly discovered vulnerabilities, patches and hardens its assets, and manages anti-malware program, thereby reducing the overall risk to acceptable levels.

This policy is intended to cover the people, processes, and technologies used in an effective operational strategy. It is also intended to assist Entegris' asset owners, information technology, operational technology, information security administrators, and building automation systems owners who hold the responsibility of managing vulnerabilities, patches, system hardening, and anti-malware. Deviations that are lesser than the policy, due to Entegris' requirements or local regulations, should be documented and maintained as an exception. This policy applies to all information and data assets, operational technology assets, information resources, and related infrastructure or application owned, managed, or administered by Entegris or owned and operated by a third-party on behalf of Entegris.

Accountable (A) / Responsible (R) is noted for each role. Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) — Accountable (A) Ensure Vulnerability Management and patch management programs are operational and effective Follow up with Business Leaders to ensure vulnerabilities are mitigated in a timely manner Communicate vulnerabilities and overall vulnerability management posture to executive leadership Cyber Security Council — Accountable (A) The Cyber Security Council is a cross-functional technology and business leadership forum responsible to: Ensure that the technology teams are working on appropriately prioritized security initiatives and in line with business requirements Assign resources to the teams impacted to remediate vulnerabilities Cyber Security Team (Vulnerability management team) — Responsible (R) Responsible for setting up asset discovery and vulnerability scans Establish vulnerability impact assessment, and prioritization guidelines Establish process to communicate vulnerabilities to the impacted asset owners, and monitor & report on remediation status IT Application owner — Responsible (R) Responsible to ensure the application is maintained with up to date (or approved) version of the software, and patches are installed in a timely manner. IT Systems owner — Responsible (R) Responsible to ensure the servers and databases are maintained with up to date (or approved) version of the software, and patches are installed in a timely manner. MOT Council — Responsible (R) Review and approve OT system hardening profiles Address and/or facilitate escalations Local Engineering (Maintenance /Automation) — Responsible (R) Identify vulnerabilities (manage OT vulnerability scanning solution) Rationalize OT vulnerabilities Mitigate OT vulnerabilities Operations Site Leader — Accountable (A) Establish and manage process to identify vulnerabilities and ensure they are mitigated or addressed

Term Definition Center of Excellence (COE) Group of core operational plant engineering experts that will set the stage for hardening profiles. Entegris Technology systems All Entegris technology assets and systems (both Hardware and Software) used in: IT and OT networks; IT and OT applications; Automation systems (i.e., PLCs, sensors, etc.); MES, supervisory applications; Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS); OT Communication protocols; Building/facilities automation systems, such card access systems, security cameras, etc. Hardening Profile Groupings of similar devices or applications that require similar system hardening tasks. Malware Hardware, firmware, or software that is intentionally included or inserted in a system for a harmful purpose. Manufacturing Network Administrator A system administrator that performs day-to-day maintenance activities on the PCN devices. Obsolete System Systems that have reached End of Life and/or no longer vendor supported. Operational Technology (OT) Programmable systems or devices that interact with (or manage systems that interact with) the physical environment. The systems / devices detect or cause a direct change through the monitoring and/or control of devices, processes, and events. System Hardening Process of eliminating a means of attack by patching vulnerabilities and turning off nonessential services. System Owner Person or organization responsible for the development, procurement, integration, modification, operation and maintenance, and/or final disposition of an information system. Vulnerability A weakness in an information system, system security procedures, internal controls, or implementation that could be exploited by a threat source. Examples include, new vulnerabilities, lack of hardening of devices, or change in the configuration of a device. Vulnerability Assessment Systematic examination of an information system or product to determine the adequacy of security measures, identify security deficiencies, provide data from which to predict the effectiveness of proposed security measures, and confirm the adequacy of such measures after implementation.

Entegris technology leadership must establish policy, standard and procedures for identification of threats and vulnerabilities and to take necessary timely actions. The Entegris Cybersecurity Team should remain current on newly released threats and vulnerabilities by subscribing to vendor and vulnerability advisory sources – based upon technologies employed within the local environment. An OT vulnerability management framework must be implemented to identify and manage vulnerabilities that may affect the safety and security of operations. The OT vulnerability management framework shall consist of the following: Defined roles and responsibilities A process for vulnerability monitoring for OT networks A process for infrastructure, application, and OT device vulnerability "scanning" (active and passive as necessary) A process for vulnerability rationalization A process for vulnerability mitigation and remediation A process for vulnerability reporting, justification, and compliance 6.1.1 Vulnerability Scanning​ Entegris shall employ a hybrid scanning solution using a combination of network scanning appliances, lightweight scanners (agents) deployed locally on assets, and third-party assessments to identify vulnerabilities in its technology assets. This approach ensures maximum asset coverage and a much higher vulnerability assessment frequency. Scanning shall be performed on both internal IP addresses and external IP addresses, security appliances, servers, and all network devices and appliances.

All identified external and internal vulnerabilities, once evaluated as 'true positives', shall be risk assessed and classified as critical, high, medium, or low risk vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities must then be rationalized and prioritized for appropriate remediation action.

Entegris Cybersecurity team must establish a process for communicating vulnerabilities, to the appropriate technology teams for necessary remedial action, and to monitor and track remediations progress. Entegris Cybersecurity team must establish acceptable Service Level Agreements (SLAs) to remediate different classes of IT vulnerabilities. A process shall be established to monitor and track remediation status of all vulnerabilities. All patches shall be obtained from trusted sources and approved by the vendor before testing and implementation. The respective technology teams must take appropriate remedial actions and implement them adhering to Entegris PMO, Change Management, and OT Management of Change processes. For vulnerabilities that cannot be rationalized and/or remediated due to either technology limitations or for other considerations, an exception should be submitted in accordance with the Entegris Exception Management Policy.

Entegris should capture information on the effectiveness of the vulnerabilities management program. Entegris shall capture details of all vulnerabilities in a central location and monitor and report their remediation status. All critical and high-risk vulnerabilities remediation statuses must be communicated to the ELT on a periodic basis, for information and further action.

In the event that a software patch is required urgently to be installed to protect Entegris systems, the Entegris Security Team shall draft and socialize an appropriate implementation plan: For all Entegris technology Systems - Patch should be installed within 24-48 hours to address the vulnerability, where practical. For OT systems: All Emergency patches should be considered as having "critical" impact rating, and the patch should be installed at the next available maintenance opportunity. For any reason if the above emergency timelines cannot be met, an exception request must be submitted, and approved by the Business Leader, in accordance with Entegris Exceptions Management policy.
Entegris technology teams must develop system hardening standards, implement tools and processes to enforce hardening rules thereby reduce security risks.

Entegris shall establish Anti-malware management process to protect its technology systems from malware attacks. Current and approved Anti-malware solution must be installed and updated on all the Entegris technology systems.

It is expected that all information technology and operational technology teams in Entegris will follow this policy requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business/Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented per Entegris Exception Management Process.

All security related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. Entegris Technology Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies will be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

6.6.1 Entegris employees, contractors, and other 3rd parties who are given Entegris technology assets for effective delivery of their work or service to Entegris, all such assets must be returned to Entegris on demand, or at the termination of their employment, contract, or agreement. 6.6.2 Entegris must establish a documented process to ensure that the return of assets is efficiently managed.

6.7.1 Entegris shall establish process to properly dispose all assets, at the end of their useful life or as determined by management. 6.7.2 Entegris must establish process to permanently delete all data from the asset’s hard drives/storage, prior to sending them for disposal. 6.7.3 A documented process must be established to ensure each asset is properly decommissioned and all data is transferred to designated storage (or destroyed permanently), and no residual data is left on assets hard-drive or in memory.

It is expected that all information technology and operational technology teams in Entegris will follow this policy requirements. Any exceptions to this policy, either partial or full, must be submitted by the designated Business/Technology Sponsor stating the compelling reasons as to why the requirements cannot be met, and what other compensating controls are there to mitigate the risk to Entegris. All exceptions must be given for a limited period, a maximum of 1 year. All exceptions must be documented per Entegris Exception Management Process.

All security related policies must be clearly communicated to all employees and third parties. IT/OT Management will coordinate with Human Resources as needed to determine appropriate new employee orientation, security training and awareness content areas. All Suppliers and contractors shall be required to abide by these security related policies.

All security related policies will be enforced using either system automated or manual controls. All users are expected to comply with these policies and promote secure computing practices. Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and legal prosecution.

Term Definition O365 Office 365 is the brand name used by Microsoft for a group of software plus services subscriptions that provides productivity software and/or related services to its subscribers. Legal Hold Process that an organization uses to preserve all forms of relevant information when litigation is reasonably anticipated. iTAR International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) is a set of United States government regulations that control the export and import of defense-related articles and services on the United States Munitions List (USML). Datacenter A data center is a facility used to house computer systems and associated components, such as telecommunications and storage systems

6.1.1 All Entegris employees will utilize Microsoft Office 365 (O365) for all work-related e-mail messaging. 6.1.1.1 Access to mail can be through the full client (Outlook) or browser-based Outlook Web App (OWA)

6.2.1 O365 mailboxes will be accessed utilizing the O365 client and/or the Outlook Web App (OWA). 6.2.2 O365 will have an active mailbox (inbox) size limit of 100GB. 6.2.3 Mailbox Size (Send/ Receive) Limits: 6.2.3.1 Users will be warned that they are approaching the storage limit of their inbox at 99GB and will be prohibited from sending at 99.5GB. 6.2.3.2 Users will be unable to receive email when the mailbox reaches 100GB. 6.2.3.2.1 Users can work with the Entegris Helpdesk to further archive/ purge email to get under the 100GB limit. 6.2.4 Send and receive messages size (w/attachments) is limited to 25MB. 6.2.5 Email less than 180 days old will be stored in the inbox. 6.2.6 Email older than 180 days will get moved automatically to the employee’s archive mailbox. 6.2.6.1 Users must be connected to Office 365 to access archived email; this means archived mail cannot be accessed if the user is not connected to the internet. 6.2.6.2 When archived messages are 3 years old, they will be automatically deleted (3-Year retention policy). Users will not be able to access email older than 3 years. Any email older than two years will be deleted and will not be restorable from backup. 6.2.6.3 The archive mailbox will have a default size of 100GB. 6.2.6.4 Users need to work with the Entegris Helpdesk to preserve any business-critical email long term (> 3 years) in an appropriate document management system as mentioned above, not in email. 6.2.7 User recoverability options: 6.2.7.1 Users will be able to recover email from the deleted items folder for up to 30 days. After 30 days email will not be recoverable. 6.2.8 Entegris does not allow the creation or retention of PST (Personal Storage File or Personal Folder Files stored locally on the PC).

If requested by HR or the Manager at the time of termination, Managers will have up to 30 days to review an employee’s email prior to permanent deletion. Email will not be forwarded. If Managers do not request access to the terminated employee’s mailbox, the 30-day deletion rule mentioned above will apply.

6.4.1 Employees identified as being part of an Entegris legal hold will be informed of their compliance obligations related to legal holds, and IT will suspend the 2-year email retention policy until such time as the legal hold is terminated. 6.4.2 Once the legal hold is removed, the 3-year email retention policy will be enforced and email older than 3 years will be automatically deleted. 6.4.3 IT will work with Legal to perform a semi-annual review for all legal hold individuals.

The email system should not be used to store restricted information, including iTAR controlled data. All data controlled by iTAR regulations should be stored on the approved corporate iTAR system/ application, where it is properly restricted and controlled.

6.6.1 Since email will be stored off site at Microsoft’s data center as a cloud provider, there is no internal Entegris email backup. Microsoft maintains their own backup and recovery environment only to ensure availability of the Office 365 application for its customers. 6.6.2 Backups cannot be used for the recovery of historical email that was deleted and surpassed the 30-day soft delete period. 6.6.3 User deleted email cannot be recovered beyond 30 days.

Shared mailboxes are used by global back-office teams like Customer Service for order taking, providing quotes, processing invoices, etc. All shared mailboxes have no archive policy. The general Inbox folder has a retention policy of 4 yrs. After 4yrs, any email from the Inbox folder will automatically be deleted.

6.8.1 In extremely rare circumstances, there could be instances where compliance and business requirements warrant the need for longer retention schedules (> 2 years). These exceptions will be handled individually and: 6.8.1.1 Will be reviewed for appropriate business justification and evidence of laws mandating the request. 6.8.1.2 Reviewed periodically to ensure that they are kept to a minimum.
Forwarding of business-related email from the Entegris corporate email environment to any personal email accounts for the purpose of bypassing the retention policy is strictly prohibited.
Any user found to have violated this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

documents.t: 1.1 To provide a framework of incident control and approved incident management for our systems environments. Entegris is a global organization that has systems deployed in North America, Europe, and Asia. Due to the geographical impact of our shared systems and their criticality to continued business operations, IT requires formal incident management policies and procedures in order to effectively and efficiently handle and resolve incidents that disrupt or degrade the normal functioning of IT services. 1.2 The goal of incident management is to restore service as quickly as possible, after an incident. The process includes the methods and actions for monitoring, discovering, reporting, and resolving incidents. The process also aims to reduce downtime and minimize impact on employee productivity from incidents. 1.3 A major incident (Priority 1) is the highest-impact, highest-urgency incident. Given the urgency of the situation, a well-coordinated response process is required to accelerate the resolution and minimize the business impact. This includes: 1.3.1 Minimize the impact of service interruptions. 1.3.2 Ensure that an appropriate Incident Manager/Major Incident Team/Management Group are in place to manage a major incident. 1.3.3 Ensure that stakeholders are well-informed of service interruptions, degradations, and resolutions. 1.3.4 Conduct a review of each major incident once service is restored. Its purpose is to analyze the incident and understand what can be done to prevent a similar incident in the future. This review also provides an opportunity to evaluate the incident response process and identify areas for improvement. 1.3.5 Create a problem for root cause analysis.

2.1 The scope of this policy is Global. 2.2 All production systems - corporate-wide used applications and infrastructure resources owned and maintained by IT, OT (when they require IT), and the business. Out-of-scope: Assets managed/maintained by Control Systems Engineering

Caller Bringing incidents to the attention of the Service Desk Participating in the implementation of a solution or workaround Confirming successful resolution Global Service Desk (Level 1) Recording, ownership, monitoring, tracking, and communication about incidents Investigating and diagnosing incidents Providing resolutions and workarounds from standard operating procedures and existing known errors Escalating incidents to IT support Communicating with the caller/end users Status updates on resolution times Major Incident Coordinator/Manager Assigned to a major incident to co-ordinate the investigation and resolution Assigns tasks to other teams to investigate and resolve the major incident Manage communications during the major incident to both business and IT stakeholders Creates ad hoc communication plans and tasks. Conducts a review of the major incident once resolved IT Support Teams (Level 2 / 3) Investigate and diagnose incidents escalated from the Service Desk Developing workarounds Resolution and recovery of assigned incidents Create incidents after detecting a service failure or quality degradation or a situation that may result in one

Term Definition Impact Measure of business criticality Incident An unplanned interruption in service ITIL Information Technology Infrastructure Library Major Incident An unplanned interruption in service of the highest priority (priority 1) Priority Product of Impact and Urgency SLA Service level agreement Urgency The extent to which resolution of the incident can bear delay

6.1 Detect, classify, prioritize, assign, communicate and resolve incidents. All incidents are reviewed by the Global Service Desk and/or support teams. Once the candidate is assigned, teams shall track SLAs to ensure resolution within the agreed timeframes. 6.2 Suggest, promote, classify, communicate, resolve, and analyze root cause for major incidents. All proposed candidates are reviewed primarily by the Major Incident Coordinator and Incident Manager. They can be accepted or rejected by choosing the relevant option in the context menu. Once the candidate is promoted to a major incident, the Major incident state field is automatically updated to Accepted and the major incident process begins. 6.3 All unplanned interruptions in service are documented in ServiceNow Incident tickets. 6.4 Incidents are classified by Category and Subcategory (required) and configuration Item if possible. 6.5 Incidents are prioritized based on Impact and Urgency. 6.6 Impacted customers are notified of incidents and progress to resolution. 6.7 Incidents are investigated and diagnosed if a resolution is not immediately available. 6.8 Non-major Incidents are resolved when service is restored (can be via a work around) and automatically closed after 3 days. 6.9 Major Incidents are resolved when service is restored (can be via a work around) and are not automatically closed. The Resolution code and Resolution notes must be entered. The Business impact and Probable cause must be entered. The Actual outage start date & time, and end date & time must be entered so the Business impact duration can be calculated. The Post Incident Report fields must be entered. Initial root cause analysis is considered complete when the Findings are entered within 10 business days 6.9.1 Note - If an incident is determined to be Cybersecurity related, the incident will be assigned to the Cybersecurity group. Cybersecurity has its own policy concerning these incidents. 6.10 Track and Report Incident Status. Maintain a tracking and reporting system to document incidents, communicate the status of in-process incidents, and completed incidents. 6.11 Open incidents shall be updated at least weekly with Additional comments (Customer visible) to facilitate communication. Work notes shall be used to document any part of the resolution process to the resolution team(s). 6.12 Open major incidents status shall be updated at least hourly within the ServiceNow ticket. 6.13 Close and document the incidents. Whenever incidents are resolved, update accordingly the solution and user documentation and the procedures affected by the resolution. 6.14 Ensure appropriate updates to all relevant documentation (SOPs, configuration, etc.). 6.15 Prioritization must be done based on Impact and Urgency matrix.

Priority Definition SLA 1 Critical (Major Incident) Significant impact on business operations and require immediate attention. For example, a complete system outage affecting multiple departments. Emergency Change: Changes that must be implemented immediately to resolve a major incident or restore a service – tend to be high risk. Response SLA 30 minutes, Resolution SLA 4 hours, Schedule 24x7 2 High Notable impact but not as severe as critical incidents. They require swift resolutions to prevent further disruption. An example could be a software bug affecting a critical business process. Response SLA 2 hours, Resolution SLA 8 hours, Schedule 24x7. 3 Moderate Moderate impact on business operations and can be resolved within a reasonable timeframe. For instance, a group experiencing intermittent connectivity issues. Response SLA 1 day, Resolution SLA 3 days, Schedule Sunday 7pm to Friday 7pm CST. 4 Low Minimal impact on business operations and can be resolved without significant disruption. A minor cosmetic issue on a non-critical webpage could be an example. Response SLA 3 days, Resolution SLA 10 days, Schedule Sunday 7pm to Friday 7pm CST.

1.1 This policy deals with the backup guidelines for critical IT systems at Entegris. 1.2 This policy is required because all systems that are critical to Entegris need to follow a reliable and regular backup schedule that is managed by either automated/ manual processes. This policy would also serve the purpose to provide guidelines for developing tape and tapeless/ disk backup procedures for all sites/ locations where backups are essential. 1.3 This policy establishes requirements related to the backup and recovery activities to protect the integrity and availability of all electronic assets.

2.1 Global. 2.2 IT understands that all systems over the entire worldwide operations do not maintain the same level of business criticality. Hence it is not essential for all sites to follow this policy on a strict basis as they may not have the resources, support and the hardware to support the needed procedures. Any deviation to the list must be approved by the business heads, according to the critical systems/ application list.

For internally hosted applications and systems, all business owners must work with IT to ensure that all critical data is appropriately backed up to ensure appropriate options in the event of an availability outage. For all applications and systems that are hosted in the cloud, the vendor relationship managers need to ensure that appropriate contract terms ensure for this. SaaS vendors are expected to assist with any disaster recovery solutions and annual tests to verify appropriate response procedures.

Reference Documents: 08569 – Creating Backup Status Report 08580 – Entegris Standard Backup Policy 08572 - Remote Backup Reports 09955 – How to Restore File from Backup (File Share Only) Special Notes: Policy # DSS04.07.501

5.1.1 All server-based production information systems (application servers, file servers and network infrastructure servers) must be backed up according to an approved backup schedule. The resource owner is responsible for the review and approval of the backup schedule. 5.1.2 The backup schedule must include the extent (full or differential) of backup, the frequency, and retention period. The backup schedule should reflect the business requirements of the organization and the security regulations of the information. 5.1.2.1 Daily Disk based Backups 5.1.2.2 Weekly Disk based Backups 5.1.2.3 Monthly Tape Backups – stored offsite 5.1.3 Backup procedures must cover all production systems, applications, and data necessary to cover the entire system in the event of disaster. 5.1.4 Invariable of backup technology (Disk based/ Tape based) all backups must be stored in a secure site at a sufficient distance away to escape any damage from disaster at the main site. 5.1.5 Backup infrastructure should be given an appropriate level of physical and environmental protection consistent with the standard applied at the main site. 5.1.6 All backup data stored offsite must be documented that shows the date when the information was most recently modified as well as the nature of the information. 5.1.7 The backup log should be reviewed and evidenced on a daily basis to confirm the success of each backup job. 5.1.8 All backup failures must be investigated and resolved within the next backup cycle. Resolution of failed backups must be documented in a IT Service Request. 5.1.9 With a few exceptions, Entegris does not provide backup of applications or data stored on personal computer hard drives or portable hard drives. Thus, data of this nature should be stored on a network group drive or other source covered by this policy.

5.2.1 File and system restoration requests and results are documented in the IT Service Management Application. 5.2.2 File and system restoration procedures should be periodically tested to validate that they are effective and that they can be completed within the time allotted in the operational procedures for recovery. 5.2.3 All files are restored back to the original/ temporary location of the data. All other requests must be approved by the resource owner. The security requirements of the data must not be compromised by providing unauthorized access to restored data.

5.3.1 In the event that Entegris contracts with a third party to host infrastructure and/or data related to a particular system, the third party must have backup and recovery procedures either equivalent to or more rigorous than Entegris’ internal procedures. 5.3.1.1 Disk Based Backups are sent to Exagrid at local site and then replicated to another Exagrid at a different site
